```
1	# Live Comp Search — 3-Layer Protocol
2	
3	The agent runs this loop in **Phase 2 (Pricing)** of Folder Mode, and in
4	**Step 2** of Text Mode, for every item being priced. Sold-anchored, multi-
5	source, date-stamped. Replaces the prior asking-only Google-snippet approach.
6	
7	Pricing math (target → list → floor → garage-sale) lives in `SKILL.md` and
8	`pricing-reference.md`. **This file is about how to find the comp numbers**,
9	not what to do with them.
10	
11	## The 3 layers, in order
12	
13	| Layer | Source | Signal | When to run |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| 1 | eBay AU sold listings | **Sold** (primary anchor) | Always when a browser is attached; else skip → lean on Layers 2–3 |
16	| 2 | FB Marketplace live search | Asking (competitor set) | Always, unless Layer 1 strong AND item < $30 |
17	| 3 | Google snippet search | Asking (last resort) | Only when Layers 1–2 combined yield <3 valid comps |
18	
19	Every layer either produces a captured block or a `skipped_reason` — never
20	silently absent. See "Recording skipped layers" at the bottom.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Layer 1 — eBay AU sold listings (primary anchor)
25	
26	### URL template
27	
28	```
29	https://www.ebay.com.au/sch/i.html?_nkw=<keywords>&LH_Sold=1&LH_Complete=1&_ipg=60
30	```
31	
32	- `LH_Sold=1` and `LH_Complete=1` together filter to **sold** listings only
33	  (without `_Sold`, `_Complete` includes unsold ended auctions).
34	- `_ipg=60` returns 60 results per page — usually enough.
35	
36	### Fetch mechanism — browser-driven (not a plain GET)
37	
38	eBay AU blocks non-browser HTTP clients: a plain WebFetch / WebSearch GET to the
39	URL above returns an Akamai **403 "Access Denied"** edge block or a
40	`splashui/challenge` interstitial — **never sold rows**. A real browser session
41	(cookies + JS) clears the challenge in ~3 s. So Layer 1 runs through the **same
42	attached Chrome (port 9222) as Layer 2**, via Chrome DevTools MCP. Unlike FB,
43	eBay's search is URL-driven — the params survive navigation, so there's no
44	searchbox to type into; you navigate straight to the URL.
45	
46	Sequence (reuse a single eBay search tab across items, like Layer 2's FB tab):
47	
48	1. `navigate_page` → the eBay sold URL above (keywords URL-encoded).
49	2. Pause **~3 s** for the `splashui/challenge` interstitial to auto-clear. Tune
50	   from 3 s: if step 3 still shows the challenge / "Access Denied" / a "checking
51	   your browser" page instead of result rows, wait once more (up to ~8 s total)
52	   or `navigate_page` reload once. If it still won't clear, that's a
53	   stop-the-line (see below) — not an empty result.
54	3. Read the resolved results page. Prefer `evaluate_script` to pull sold rows
55	   straight from the DOM — more reliable than the a11y snapshot for a dense
56	   result grid. As of this writing eBay AU renders each result as `li.s-card`
57	   (older layout: `li.s-item`): title in `.s-card__title` (`.s-item__title`),
58	   price in `.s-card__price` (`.s-item__price`), sold date in the card's
59	   caption / "Sold <date>" signal line (feeds the recency filter below).
60	   **Skip the first card** — eBay seeds a hidden "Shop on eBay" template row.
61	   Take the first price per card (the sold price) and parse the leading number
62	   from strings like "AU $44.49" or a range "AU $20 to AU $40". Selectors
63	   drift: if a parse returns **zero rows while the page clearly shows results**,
64	   that's stale selectors — re-derive them from a fresh snapshot, don't record
65	   0 comps.
66	4. Parse median / min / max / count from the sold prices, then apply the recency
67	   filter, outlier trim, and captures schema below — all unchanged.
68	
69	### Run-budget rules (rate-limit hygiene)
70	
71	- **8–15 s random pause between eBay searches** in a single run — same cadence
72	  as Layer 2's FB pause, because Layer 1 now shares the same browser and the
73	  same rate-limit surface.
74	- **No hard per-run search cap** (unlike Layer 2's 20-FB-search cap): eBay
75	  search is read-only and not tied to the logged-in account that posts, so the
76	  ban consequence is lower. The pause is the primary hygiene; a block that
77	  recurs across several items is the rate-limit signal — escalate via
78	  stop-the-line (below) rather than enforcing a fixed count.
79	- Same **stop-the-line conditions** as Layer 2 and the listing-creation loop
80	  (`browser-automation.md` § Stop-the-line). The transient ~3 s challenge that
81	  clears itself is normal; a block that *persists* after a reload, a captcha, a
82	  "browsing too fast" warning, or a login wall → screenshot + surface to the
83	  user, stop the search loop. Do not retry-search.
84	
85	### No attached browser (Text Mode without Chrome)
86	
87	This path is reachable in **Text Mode only** — Folder and Refresh Mode hard-gate
88	on an attached Chrome at Phase 0 and abort before pricing, so Layer 1 always has
89	a browser there.
90	
91	Layer 1 needs the browser. With no attached Chrome, **do not fall back to a
92	plain GET** — it returns the 403 / challenge page, never comps, so a
93	"best-effort" GET is just a guaranteed-empty request that risks misparsing the
94	block page as data. Instead record `skipped_reason: "no_browser_session"` on
95	`ebay_sold` (the same value Layer 2 uses) and lean on Layers 2–3, applying the
96	asking→sold gap (×0.80) to the asking-side anchor. Comp confidence drops
97	accordingly.
98	
99	### Optional refinements
100	
101	- `&_sop=13` — sort by ended most recently. Use when the default relevance
102	  ranking surfaces stale items.
103	- `&LH_PrefLoc=1` — restrict to AU-located sellers only. Use for items where
104	  locality affects price (furniture, large appliances, bikes). Skip for small
105	  shippable items where AU vs international doesn't change the realised price.
106	
107	### Keyword crafting
108	
109	Brand + model + key spec. **No condition words** ("used", "good cond"). eBay's
110	sold filter already implies real transactions. Examples:
111	
112	- `Mongoose 20 inch kids mountain bike`
113	- `Weber Q1200 bbq`
114	- `IKEA Lappljung Ruta rug 200x300`
115	- `Enrico student violin 1/2`
116	
117	### Recency filter
118	
119	eBay's sold listings persist for ~90 days. Discard any sold result older than
120	**60 days** from today — the market shifts and stale sales mislead.
121	
122	### Outlier trim
123	
124	- `n ≥ 10`: trim top and bottom 10th percentile before computing median.
125	- `3 ≤ n < 10`: drop a single extreme outlier if it's >2× the median or
126	  <0.5× the median.
127	- `n < 3`: keep all, but mark `comp_confidence: "low"` downstream.
128	
129	### What counts as a strong Layer-1 anchor
130	
131	`n ≥ 3` post-trim **AND** at least 2 results within one condition tier of the
132	item being priced (see `pricing-reference.md` for the condition ladder).
133	
134	### Captures
135	
136	Write to the run-state `comps.ebay_sold` block:
137	
138	```
139	{
140	  "median": <int AUD>,
141	  "min": <int AUD>,
142	  "max": <int AUD>,
143	  "count": <int post-trim>,
144	  "window_days": 60,
145	  "search_url": "<full URL>",
146	  "skipped_reason": null
147	}
148	```
149	
150	---
151	
152	## Layer 2 — FB Marketplace live (asking-side competitor set)
153	
154	FB Marketplace search is **client-rendered** — no URL params survive a
155	navigation. The agent must drive the browser via Chrome DevTools MCP on the
156	attached Chrome (port 9222). See `browser-automation.md` for general
157	pre-conditions; this layer reuses the same login session.
158	
159	### Navigation sequence
160	
161	1. `navigate_page` → `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/melbourne/search`
162	   (Melbourne-scoped search route. If FB shows a different default city,
163	   change it once in the UI — the agent doesn't manage the city setting.)
164	2. `take_snapshot` to find the search input (role: `searchbox`, name: "Search
165	   Marketplace" or similar).
166	3. `click` the searchbox UID → `press_key("ctrl+a")` → `fill(<keywords>)`.
167	   The same field-replace quirk from `facebook-marketplace.md` applies — fill
168	   appends without the select-all first.
169	4. `press_key("Enter")`. Wait ~1 s for the result grid to populate.
170	5. `take_snapshot` of the grid. Extract the first **15–20 cards**: title,
171	   price, location, posted-at relative time if visible.
172	6. Confirm the location filter is **Melbourne or Melbourne region**. If FB
173	   has auto-widened to "Australia" or another city, record
174	   `skipped_reason: "wrong_location"` and move on — do not adjust filters.
175	
176	### When to run
177	
178	- **Always**, except: Layer 1 anchor is strong AND the item's expected target
179	  price is < $30. (Browser time isn't free for sub-$30 items.)
180	- When Layer 1 is strong, timebox Layer 2 to **20 s** — it's a sanity check,
181	  not a decision input.
182	
183	### Captures
184	
185	```
186	{
187	  "median": <int AUD>,
188	  "min": <int AUD>,
189	  "max": <int AUD>,
190	  "count": <int>,
191	  "query": "<keywords>",
192	  "skipped_reason": null
193	}
194	```
195	
196	### Run-budget rules
197	
198	- **8–15 s random pause** between FB searches in a single run.
199	- Cap **20 FB searches per run**. Folders with >20 priced items batch into a
200	  second run with a ≥30 min gap.
201	- Reuse a single Marketplace search tab across items — don't open a new tab
202	  per item.
203	- Same stop-the-line conditions as the listing-creation loop:
204	  captcha / login wall / "browsing too fast" warning → screenshot + surface
205	  to the user, stop the search loop. Do not retry-search.
206	
207	### Sponsored / off-topic cards
208	
209	FB doesn't always label sponsored slots. If the first 20 cards are mostly
210	off-topic for the keywords (e.g. searching "Mongoose kids bike" returns adult
211	bikes), scroll the grid once and re-snapshot. If still off-topic, record
212	`count: <n on-topic>` and `skipped_reason: null` — partial signal is fine,
213	just honest.
214	
215	---
216	
217	## Layer 3 — Google snippet fallback
218	
219	Only fires when Layers 1–2 **combined** produce <3 valid comps (e.g. genuinely
220	niche or discontinued items).
221	
222	Existing search patterns:
223	
224	- `<brand model> facebook marketplace australia`
225	- `<brand model> ebay australia used`
226	- `used <item type> price australia`
227	
228	Extract any concrete price mentions from snippets. Confidence is auto-
229	downgraded to `"low"` when Layer 3 is the anchor source — Google snippets
230	mix new RRP, US prices, and old listings without distinguishing them.
231	
232	### Captures
233	
234	```
235	{
236	  "ran": true,
237	  "notes": "<1-line description of what was found>"
238	}
239	```
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Comp validity rules (recap)
244	
245	Full rules and condition ladder live in `pricing-reference.md` (section: "What
246	counts as a valid comp"). The short version:
247	
248	- **Recency** — eBay sold ≤60 d; FB live is current by definition.
249	- **Condition match** — same tier preferred; one tier away OK without
250	  adjustment; two tiers away only as last signal, with tier-step adjustment.
251	  Unknown condition → treat as "good", mark `condition: unknown`.
252	- **Title match** — brand + item-type token both required. Reject same-brand-
253	  different-product (e.g. adult Mongoose when pricing a kids bike).
254	- **Outlier trim** — see Layer 1 rules.
255	- **Free listings ($0)** — excluded everywhere.
256	- **n<3 anywhere** → `comp_confidence: "low"`; the agent says so plainly in
257	  the seller-notes block.
258	
259	---
260	
261	## Recording skipped layers (auditability)
262	
263	A `comps` block in run-state always contains all three layer keys. When a
264	layer doesn't run, populate `skipped_reason`:
265	
266	| `skipped_reason` value | Meaning |
267	|---|---|
268	| `"sub_30_strong_anchor"` | Layer 1 strong + item < $30 → Layer 2 skipped |
269	| `"layers_1_to_2_sufficient"` | Layers 1–2 combined ≥ 3 → Layer 3 (Google) skipped |
270	| `"no_browser_session"` | Text Mode without attached Chrome → Layer 1 and/or Layer 2 skipped (both are browser-driven) |
271	| `"wrong_location"` | FB widened scope past Melbourne region |
272	| `"stop_the_line"` | Captcha / login wall / rate-limit — see browser-automation.md |
273	| `"zero_results"` | Layer ran but returned nothing on-topic |
274	
275	Same shape in `listing.md` `## Comps` — write `- skipped (<reason>)` under the
276	heading rather than dropping the heading.
277	
278	---
279	
280	## Common rationalisations to reject
281	
282	| Rationalisation | Why it fails |
283	|---|---|
284	| "eBay sold via WebFetch came back empty — Layer 1 has no comps, skip it." | WebFetch can't clear eBay's bot challenge (it returns a 403 / `splashui` page, not rows). That's the wrong tool, not "no comps." Drive Layer 1 through the attached Chrome. |
285	| "eBay had n=0 — I'll just use the asking median as the target." | Apply the asking→sold gap (×0.80). Asking median ≠ realised price; ignoring the gap is what the prior protocol got wrong. |
286	| "I'll skip Layer 2 — Layer 1 was strong." | Only skip Layer 2 when target < $30. Above $30, Layer 2 catches stale-sold / live-market divergence (sanity-check role). |
287	| "The first 20 FB cards looked off-topic — I'll just write count=0." | Scroll and re-snapshot once before giving up. Partial on-topic count is more honest than abandoning the layer. |
288	| "I'll skip the 8–15 s pause between FB searches — the listing-creation delay is what matters." | Read traffic also triggers rate limits on Marketplace search. Burst searching can captcha the same account that's about to post listings. |
```

{
  "function": "() => {\n  const cards = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('li.s-card, li.s-item'));\n  const out = [];\n  for (const c of cards) {\n    const t = c.querySelector('.s-card__title, .s-item__title');\n    const p = c.querySelector('.s-card__price, .s-item__price');\n    const cap = c.querySelector('.s-card__caption, .s-item__caption, .s-item__title--tagblock');\n    if (!t || !p) continue;\n    out.push({title: t.innerText.trim(), price: p.innerText.trim(), cap: cap ? cap.innerText.trim() : ''});\n  }\n  return {count: out.length, rows: out.slice(0, 40), title: document.title};\n}"
}

{
  "function": "() => {\n  const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[href*=\"/marketplace/item/\"]'));\n  const out = [];\n  const seen = new Set();\n  for (const a of links) {\n    const txt = a.innerText.trim();\n    if (!txt) continue;\n    const m = txt.match(/A?U?\\$[\\d,]+/);\n    if (!m) continue;\n    const price = parseInt(m[0].replace(/[^\\d]/g,''),10);\n    const key = txt.slice(0,60);\n    if (seen.has(key)) continue;\n    seen.add(key);\n    out.push({price, txt: txt.replace(/\\n/g,' | ').slice(0,120)});\n  }\n  return {count: out.length, rows: out.slice(0,25)};\n}"
}

1	# Facebook Marketplace — Field Map & Listing Guide
2	
3	## Create listing URL
4	
5	```
6	https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/create/item
7	```
8	
9	Log in must be active in the attached Chrome before navigating here. If you
10	land on a login wall, stop and surface the issue to the user (see
11	`browser-automation.md` stop-the-line conditions).
12	
13	## Marketplace search (read-only — comp lookup)
14	
15	For **Phase 2 comp searches** the agent uses Marketplace search, not the
16	create-listing form. The URL is client-rendered, so query terms must be
17	typed into the searchbox rather than passed as URL params:
18	
19	```
20	https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/melbourne/search
21	```
22	
23	Full navigation sequence (snapshot → click searchbox → ctrl+a → fill → Enter
24	→ snapshot grid → extract cards), run-budget rules (8–15 s pause between
25	searches, cap 20/run), and skipped-layer recording live in
26	`live-comp-search.md` (Layer 2).
27	
28	Same stop-the-line conditions apply (captcha, login wall, "browsing too
29	fast") — see the table at the bottom of this file.
30	
31	## Field fill order
32	
33	FB Marketplace validates fields progressively — fill in this order to avoid
34	state errors:
35	
36	1. **Photos** — upload first; the form won't let you change category until at
37	   least one photo is present on some variants of the form.
38	2. **Category** — select from the category mapping table below.
39	3. **Title** — from the approved ad copy.
40	4. **Price** — AUD, numbers only (no `$` sign — the field adds currency).
41	5. **Condition** — see condition mapping table below.
42	6. **Description** — from the approved ad copy.
43	7. **Location** — type suburb; select the autocomplete suggestion. Do not
44	   free-type the full address.
45	8. **"Hide from friends" toggle** — leave at user's current default (do not
46	   change this setting; it varies by account preference).
47	
48	After filling Location, the form typically shows a preview / "Next" button
49	leading to the review screen. Snapshot to confirm you're on the review screen
50	before stopping.
51	
52	## Photo rules
53	
54	- Maximum **10 photos** per listing (free accounts). Do not attempt an 11th
55	  upload — FB may silently drop it or show an error.
56	- First photo uploaded becomes the **lead/cover photo** in search results.
57	  Upload in lexical filename order so the user controls ordering by naming
58	  files `01-front.jpg`, `02-side.jpg`, etc.
59	- Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, HEIC. Minimum resolution: 500 × 500 px.
60	  Maximum file size: 10 MB per photo.
61	- Do not upload watermarked, AI-generated, or stock photos — image similarity
62	  detection will flag the listing.
63	
64	## Category mapping
65	
66	Use the closest match. FB's category tree changes occasionally; re-snapshot
67	after selecting a top-level category to confirm the subcategory options.
68	
69	| Item type | Top-level | Subcategory |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| Furniture (sofa, table, chair, shelf) | Home & Garden | Furniture |
72	| Appliances (washing machine, fridge) | Home & Garden | Appliances |
73	| Small appliances (blender, toaster) | Home & Garden | Household items |
74	| Garden / outdoor furniture | Home & Garden | Outdoor |
75	| TVs, monitors | Electronics | TVs & Video |
76	| Computers, laptops | Electronics | Computers & Tablets |
77	| Phones | Electronics | Phones |
78	| Audio (speakers, headphones) | Electronics | Audio |
79	| Power tools | Tools | Power Tools |
80	| Hand tools | Tools | Hand Tools |
81	| Bikes (push bikes) | Sporting Goods | Bikes |
82	| Exercise equipment | Sporting Goods | Exercise & Fitness |
83	| Kids / baby gear | Baby & Kids | Baby & Toddler Gear |
84	| Kids' footwear / sports boots | Sporting Goods | Sports & Outdoors |
85	| Clothing, shoes (adult) | Clothing & Accessories | (match gender/type) |
86	| Books, music, games | Entertainment | Books, Movies & Music |
87	| Cars, utes, vans | Vehicles | Cars & Trucks |
88	| BBQs, outdoor cooking | Home & Garden | Outdoor |
89	| Camera / photography | Electronics | Cameras |
90	
91	If an item doesn't fit cleanly, prefer the broader top-level category over an
92	incorrect subcategory — buyers search the top level more often.
93	
94	## Condition mapping
95	
96	| User's condition | FB condition field value |
97	|---|---|
98	| New / sealed | New |
99	| Like new / barely used | Used - Like New |
100	| Good condition | Used - Good |
101	| Fair / some wear | Used - Fair |
102	| For parts / broken | Used - For Parts |
103	
104	Do not select "New" for any item that has been opened, even if unused.
105	
106	## Captcha / login-wall / 2FA handling
107	
108	- **Login wall on navigate**: session expired. Screenshot + stop. User must
109	  log in again in the browser.
110	- **"Confirm your identity" / checkpoint screen**: a Meta security check.
111	  Screenshot + stop. User must complete it. Do not retry.
112	- **Photo upload captcha**: rare but occurs on new accounts or burst uploads.
113	  Screenshot + stop.
114	- **"You're temporarily blocked from listing"**: rate-limit. Screenshot + stop.
115	  Tell the user to wait at least 1 hour (Meta's typical block window) before
116	  continuing.
117	
118	## Ban-avoidance hygiene
119	
120	These reduce (not eliminate) the risk of account action:
121	
122	- **One listing at a time, 30–90 s apart.** Never post multiple items in rapid
123	  succession.
124	- **Don't list more than ~5–10 items per week from a new account.** Older
125	  accounts with transaction history tolerate higher volumes.
126	- **Real photos only.** Stock / AI-generated images trigger image classifiers.
127	- **No phone numbers or external URLs in the description.** FB strips them and
128	  the listing may be demoted or rejected.
129	- **Accurate category.** Miscategorised listings get flagged by other users and
130	  may be removed.
131	- **Don't relist the same item within 7 days.** Even if you delete and
132	  repost, FB's hashing catches it.
133	- **Use the pickup location accurately.** Mismatched locations (profile address
134	  vs. listing suburb) are a soft signal.
135	- **Hide from friends** — this is a per-listing toggle. Some users prefer it
136	  on to avoid acquaintances seeing everything they sell; leave at the user's
137	  existing default.
138	
139	## Known fill quirks (discovered in testing — read before Phase 4)
140	
141	These are not in the accessibility tree docs. Each was found through a failed
142	attempt during a real run; baked in here to avoid repeating them.
143	
144	- **Title and price fields append, not replace.** `fill()` appends to the
145	  existing placeholder or previous value. The native value setter approach
146	  throws "Illegal invocation" on FB's React fiber. Use this sequence instead:
147	  1. `click(uid)` — focus the field
148	  2. `press_key("ctrl+a")` — select all existing content
149	  3. `fill(value)` — type the new value (replaces selection)
150	  4. `evaluate_script` to read back the field value and confirm it matches.
151	  If the readback doesn't match, repeat once before escalating.
152	
153	- **Description textarea requires click then type_text.** `fill()` alone does
154	  not persist in the Sports & Outdoors (and some other) category forms.
155	  Correct sequence: `click(uid)` → `type_text(text)`. Verify the value was
156	  accepted: `document.querySelectorAll('textarea')[0].value`.
157	
158	- **Location autocomplete: use keyboard, not snapshot click.** The autocomplete
159	  suggestions often do not appear in the a11y tree even though they exist in
160	  the DOM. Reliable sequence: JS-clear the location field → `fill("suburb")` →
161	  `press_key("ArrowDown")` → `press_key("Enter")`. This reliably selects the
162	  first suggestion.
163	
164	- **Photos must be in an MCP-accessible path.** The `upload_file` MCP tool
165	  only allows files within the workspace roots. `/tmp/` is NOT accessible —
166	  it will return "Access denied". Use the system temp dir instead:
167	  ```bash
168	  cp /path/to/photo.jpg /var/folders/jd/9__6t9p9725glsmql48869lh0000gn/T/photo.jpg
169	  ```
170	  The accessible temp path is discovered in Phase 0: run `evaluate_script`
171	  with `os.tmpdir()` or check the MCP workspace roots list for a path matching
172	  `/var/folders/*/T`. Store it in the run-state for the whole run. If the
173	  path is unknown, copy a test file and confirm the upload succeeds before
174	  staging all photos.
175	
176	- **Post-publish success signal — poll, don't `wait_for`.** After clicking
177	  Publish, FB navigates either to the listing detail page (URL contains
178	  `/marketplace/item/<id>`) or, on some A/B variants, to a your-listings page
179	  (`/marketplace/you/selling` or `/marketplace/your_listings`).
180	  Do NOT use `wait_for` for this — it matches text content, not URL changes,
181	  and will never resolve. Poll `window.location.href` via `evaluate_script`
182	  every 500 ms for up to 15 s and match against the URL patterns above.
183	  Full protocol (success paths, redirect fallback, timeout handling) lives in
184	  `browser-automation.md` Step 6.
185	
186	### Listing-URL recovery via Selling-page iframe
187	
188	When the post-publish poll lands on the your-listings page or times out, the
189	real `/marketplace/item/<id>/` URL is not in the address bar — but it is
190	embedded in the ad-preview iframe FB renders at the bottom of the filtered
191	Selling page (`/marketplace/you/selling?title_search=<URL-encoded title>`).
192	The iframe's `src` carries a URL-encoded `creative_spec` JSON blob whose
193	`object_story_spec.link_data.link` is the real listing URL and whose `.name`
194	is the listing title.
195	
196	Note: the `target_id=...` param on the row's `Promote now` link looks like a
197	listing ID but is FB's **ad-targeting** ID, not the marketplace listing ID —
198	do not build a listing URL from it. The `creative_spec.link` below is the
199	only reliable source on this page.
200	
201	Canonical extractor (the `browser-automation.md` Step 6b `evaluate_script`
202	body):
203	
204	```js
205	() => {
206	  const f = document.querySelector('iframe[src*="ads/ad_preview_generator_iframe"]');
207	  if (!f || !f.src) return null;
208	  const m = f.src.match(/[?&]creative_spec=([^&]+)/);
209	  if (!m) return null;
210	  try {
211	    const spec = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(m[1]));
212	    const ld = spec.object_story_spec.link_data;
213	    if (!ld || typeof ld.link !== 'string' || typeof ld.name !== 'string') return null;
214	    return { url: ld.link, name: ld.name };
215	  } catch (e) {
216	    return null;
217	  }
218	}
219	```
220	
221	**Identity verification is mandatory.** The returned `name` must match the
222	title just published **exactly** (after trimming surrounding whitespace)
223	before the URL is trusted — two listings published in quick succession can
224	surface the wrong row's iframe first, and the name match is the only guard
225	against attributing a URL to the wrong item. Don't loosen the match beyond a
226	trim.
227	
228	**DOM brittleness.** This depends on FB keeping the ad-preview iframe and the
229	`creative_spec` shape. If either changes, the extractor returns `null` and
230	the existing operator-paste fallback (`your_listings_redirect` /
231	`timeout_manual`) kicks in unchanged — no silent wrong URL.
232	
233	## Delete listing locators (Refresh Mode Phase R1)
234	
235	FB Marketplace **does not expose a delete affordance on the public
236	listing detail page** (`/marketplace/item/<id>/`) — only `Edit`,
237	`Share`, `Mark out of stock`, and `Promote now` are present in the
238	seller's view of their own listing. The `Edit listing` page
239	(`/marketplace/edit/?listing_id=<id>`) also has no Delete button.
240	
241	The delete affordance lives **only on the Your-Listings page**
242	(`/marketplace/you/selling/`), accessed per listing row via a
243	"More options" button that opens a `popup="dialog"` menu.
244	
245	### Locating the target row
246	
247	The seller's listings page supports a server-side title filter via
248	URL query param:
249	
250	```
251	https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/you/selling?title_search=<URL-encoded title>
252	```
253	
254	Use this rather than scrolling — the Selling page lazy-loads listings
255	and the target may be far down. The Phase 4 listing title (from
256	`listing.md` `**Title:**` line) is the natural filter input.
257	
258	Single-result narrowing usually works because the listing title is
259	unique within a seller's set. If multiple rows match (e.g. the user
260	listed the same item twice), identify the correct row via its
261	ad-preview iframe: the page renders one `ads/ad_preview_generator_iframe`
262	per row, and each iframe's `creative_spec.link_data.link` contains the
263	real listing URL. Extract them with:
264	
265	```js
266	Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('iframe[src*="ads/ad_preview_generator_iframe"]'))
267	  .map(f => {
268	    const m = f.src.match(/[?&]creative_spec=([^&]+)/);
269	    if (!m) return null;
270	    try {
271	      const spec = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(m[1]));
272	      const ld = spec.object_story_spec.link_data;
273	      return ld ? { url: ld.link, name: ld.name } : null;
274	    } catch (e) { return null; }
275	  })
276	```
277	
278	Pick the row whose returned `url` matches the listing URL stored in
279	`listing.md`. Note: the `target_id=…` param on each row's `Promote
280	now` link looks like a listing ID but is FB's **ad-targeting** ID —
281	do not use it for row identification (see "Listing-URL recovery via
282	Selling-page iframe" above).
283	
284	### Menu and confirm-dialog patterns
285	
286	The locators below are all label-driven (a11y tree), not CSS — DOM
287	classes change quarterly but accessible-name conventions on FB
288	Marketplace are stable.
289	
290	| Step | Selector pattern (accessible name) | Role | Notes |
291	|---|---|---|---|
292	| 1. Open menu | `"More options for <listing title>"` | button, `expandable haspopup="dialog"` | Per-row affordance on `/marketplace/you/selling/`. |
293	| 2. Click Delete | `"Delete listing"` | menuitem | Inside the menu that opens. Other items: `Renew`, `Mark as pending`, `View listing`, `List in more places`, `Edit listing`, `View messages`. |
294	| 3. First confirm | `"Delete"` | button | In modal `dialog "Delete listing"`. Cancel button is sibling. The modal verifies title + price before this click — read them and check against the expected listing before clicking. |
295	| 4. Second-stage radio | `"No, haven't sold"` | radio | FB shows a follow-up `"Did you sell this item?"` step. For refresh-mode the truthful answer is "No, haven't sold" (not "Yes, sold …"). |
296	| 5. Submit | `"Next"` | button | Disabled until a radio is selected. After click, the modal closes and the listing row disappears from the selling page. |
297	
298	The Phase R1 sub-section in `browser-automation.md` describes the
299	end-to-end loop using these locators, including the snapshot-before-
300	every-click rule and the 15s deletion-verification poll.
301	
302	### Native Renew menu item (signal for future variant)
303	
304	The `More options` menu also exposes a `Renew` menuitem with a
305	disabled state of the form `"Renew (N days)"` until the cooldown
306	elapses (FB allows Renew every 7 days). This is the no-data-loss
307	alternative to delete-and-relist that the parent design (ABA-152)
308	explicitly defers as a future `--use-renew` variant. Locator
309	captured here so the variant can wire it later without re-exploring:
310	
311	```
312	menuitem "Renew (N days)"  // disabled when cooldown still in effect
313	menuitem "Renew"           // enabled when ready
314	```
315	
316	### Deletion-verification signals
317	
318	After clicking the second-stage `Next` button, navigating the OLD
319	listing URL (`/marketplace/item/<id>/`) produces both signals in
320	parallel — either alone is sufficient for the 15s poll:
321	
322	| Signal | Evidence | Detection key |
323	|---|---|---|
324	| URL redirect | `window.location.href` becomes `…/marketplace/melbourne/?unavailable_product=1` (the `unavailable_product=1` query param is added by FB; pathname is no longer `/marketplace/item/<id>/`) | `delete_detection: "redirect"` |
325	| Listing-gone copy | `document.body.innerText` contains "no longer available" or "isn't available" | `delete_detection: "listing_gone_copy"` |
326	
327	The `unavailable_product=1` query param is the cleanest single test —
328	if it appears, the listing is confirmed deleted. The detail-page →
329	redirect happens server-side, so the poll has to handle navigation
330	within the 15s budget (don't `wait_for` here, same reason as Phase 4
331	Step 6 — text-based wait won't catch the URL change).
332	
333	## DOM stability notes
334	
335	FB Marketplace's DOM changes frequently (sometimes monthly during A/B tests).
336	The accessibility tree snapshot is the reliable interaction layer — never
337	hardcode element IDs or CSS classes.
338	
339	Known volatile areas:
340	- The photos upload element changes between `input[type=file]` and a custom
341	  component; always locate it from the snapshot's file-input UID.
342	- The category dropdown sometimes renders as a searchable text field; if the
343	  snapshot shows a text input, type the category name and select from the
344	  autocomplete.
345	- The price field sometimes adds a currency prefix automatically; don't
346	  double-enter the `$`.
347	
348	If the snapshot doesn't match expectations: stop, screenshot, ask the user to
349	confirm the new layout before proceeding (see `browser-automation.md` Step 2).
350	
```

{
  "function": "() => {\n  const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input'));\n  const r = {};\n  for (const i of inputs) {\n    const lbl = i.getAttribute('aria-label') || i.name || '';\n    if (/title/i.test(lbl)) r.title = i.value;\n    if (/price/i.test(lbl)) r.price = i.value;\n  }\n  return r;\n}"
}

}

id: toolu_012jJ58t1fDcNjeZfxMvYqUJ
```json
{
  "function": "() => {\n  const r = {};\n  const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input'));\n  for (const i of inputs) {\n    const l = (i.getAttribute('aria-label')||'').toLowerCase();\n    if (l.includes('title')) r.title = i.value;\n    if (l.includes('price')) r.price = i.value;\n    if (l.includes('brand')) r.brand = i.value;\n    if (l.includes('location')) r.location = i.value;\n  }\n  const ta = document.querySelector('textarea');\n  r.description = ta ? ta.value : Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[contenteditable=\"true\"]')).map(e=>e.innerText)[0];\n  // checkbox states\n  r.checkboxes = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role=checkbox]')).map(c => ({name: c.getAttribute('aria-label')||'', checked: c.getAttribute('aria-checked')}));\n  return r;\n}"
}
```

```json
{
  "command": "cd ~/Desktop/things-for-sale && python3 -c \"\nimport os, re, json, uuid\nbase = os.path.expanduser('~/Desktop/things-for-sale')\n\n# Step 1 items (re-derive)\nitems = []\nfor d in sorted(os.listdir(base)):\n    lm = os.path.join(base, d, 'listing.md')\n    if not os.path.isfile(lm): continue\n    t = open(lm, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()\n    sm = re.search(r'\\*\\*Status:\\*\\*\\s*(\\w+)', t)\n    if not sm or sm.group(1) not in ('Published','Sold'): continue\n    tm = re.search(r'\\*\\*Title:\\*\\*\\s*(.+)', t)\n    pm = re.search(r'\\*\\*Price:\\*\\*[^\\d]*([\\d,]+)', t)\n    if not tm or not pm: continue\n    price = pm.group(1).replace(',','')\n    if not price.isdigit(): continue\n    items.append({'title': tm.group(1).strip(), 'price': price})\n\n# Step 2 read tracker\ntpath = os.path.join(base, 'tracker.json')\nexisting = []\nif os.path.exists(tpath):\n    existing = json.load(open(tpath, encoding='utf-8'))\nexisting_names = {str(r.get('name','')).strip().lower() for r in existing}\n\n# Step 3 append missing\nadded = []\nreport = []\nfor it in items:\n    key = it['title'].strip().lower()\n    if key in existing_names:\n        report.append((it['title'], it['price'], 'already in tracker'))\n    else:\n        new = {'id': uuid.uuid4().hex[:8], 'name': it['title'], 'listed': it['price'], 'sold': ''}\n        existing.append(new)\n        existing_names.add(key)\n        added.append(new)\n        report.append((it['title'], it['price'], 'yes'))\n\nif added:\n    with open(tpath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n        json.dump(existing, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)\n        f.write('\\n')\n\nprint('ADDED', len(added), 'of', len(items), 'parsed; tracker now has', len(existing), 'rows')\nprint('---')\nfor t,p,s in report:\n    if s != 'already in tracker':\n        print('NEW  | \\$%s | %s' % (p, t))\nprint('--- (already present: %d)' % sum(1 for _,_,s in report if s=='already in tracker'))\n\"",
  "description": "Dedup against tracker.json and append missing items"
}

{
  "command": "cd ~/Desktop/things-for-sale && python3 -c \"\nimport os, re, json\nbase = os.path.expanduser('~/Desktop/things-for-sale')\nfolders = [\n    'street-fighter-ps5',\n    'the-last-of-us-series-ps4',\n    'kids-scooters',\n    'ghost-of-yotei-ps5',\n    'canon-digital-ixus-900-ti--PowerShot SD900-camera',\n]\ntitles_to_remove = set()\nresults = []\nfor d in folders:\n    lm = os.path.join(base, d, 'listing.md')\n    if not os.path.isfile(lm):\n        results.append((d, 'NO listing.md - SKIPPED')); continue\n    t = open(lm, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()\n    tm = re.search(r'\\*\\*Title:\\*\\*\\s*(.+)', t)\n    if tm: titles_to_remove.add(tm.group(1).strip().lower())\n    sm = re.search(r'(\\*\\*Status:\\*\\*\\s*)(\\w+)', t)\n    old = sm.group(2) if sm else '?'\n    new_t = re.sub(r'(\\*\\*Status:\\*\\*\\s*)\\w+', r'\\g<1>Sold', t, count=1)\n    open(lm, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(new_t)\n    results.append((d, 'Status %s -> Sold; title=\\\"%s\\\"' % (old, tm.group(1).strip() if tm else '?')))\n\nprint('=== listing.md updates ===')\nfor d, r in results: print(' ', d, '|', r)\n\n# tracker.json removal\ntpath = os.path.join(base, 'tracker.json')\ntracker = json.load(open(tpath, encoding='utf-8'))\nbefore = len(tracker)\nremoved = [r for r in tracker if str(r.get('name','')).strip().lower() in titles_to_remove]\nkept = [r for r in tracker if str(r.get('name','')).strip().lower() not in titles_to_remove]\nwith open(tpath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n    json.dump(kept, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False); f.write('\\n')\nprint('=== tracker.json ===')\nprint('rows %d -> %d (removed %d)' % (before, len(kept), len(removed)))\nfor r in removed: print('  REMOVED:', r['name'], '(\\$%s)' % r.get('listed',''))\n\"",
  "description": "Mark 5 listings Sold and remove their tracker rows"
}

3	When the user runs `/resell-au refresh <folder>`, the skill enters
4	**Refresh Mode** — a third top-level mode alongside Text Mode and
5	Folder Mode. Refresh Mode delete-and-relists stale FB Marketplace
6	listings to reset the FB algorithm's "honeymoon" visibility window.
7	
8	This file is the single home for refresh-only reference detail. Phase
9	index (all sections live below):
10	
11	| Phase | What it does | Where to read |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| R0 | Discovery & classification (read-only) — candidate table, session cap, floor gate | § "Phase R0 — discovery & classification" |
14	| R1 | Delete existing listing on FB | `browser-automation.md` § "Refresh Mode — Phase R1 delete loop"; locators in `facebook-marketplace.md` § "Delete listing locators" |
15	| R2 | Recreate at new price + update `listing.md` | § "Phase R2 — recreate at new price"; scripts: `refresh_listing_md_update.py`, `refresh_pricing.py` |
16	| Multi-item loop | Session cap, inter-item delays, resume on restart | § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop"; script: `refresh_runstate.py` |
17	| R3 | Summary table | § "Phase R3 — summary output" |
18	
19	## Why delete-and-relist
20	
21	FB Marketplace gives every new listing a 24–48 hour "honeymoon" of
22	aggressive feed visibility. After a few days, visibility drops sharply.
23	The established reseller tactic — confirmed across 2024–2026
24	reseller-community research — is to **delete the stale listing and
25	recreate it with a fresh price.** Empirically this produces a ~30%
26	message-rate lift vs the native "Renew" button.
27	
28	Trade-off: deleting loses **saves, chat history, and view count.** The
29	skill prints a one-line data-loss warning at the top of Phase R0 so
30	the user is reminded before confirming the candidate table.
31	
32	## Phase R0 — discovery & classification
33	
34	Phase R0 is read-only: walk the target folder, parse each subfolder's
35	`listing.md`, and produce a candidate table. No browser actions in
36	this phase other than the existing Chrome login check from Folder Mode
37	Phase 0.
38	
39	### Trigger
40	
41	```
42	/resell-au refresh <folder>
43	```
44	
45	If no folder is given, default to `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`.
46	
47	### Classification rules
48	
49	For each subfolder (skip names starting with `.` or `_`):
50	
51	| Condition | Classification | In table? |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| no `listing.md` | `not-published` | silent skip |
54	| `**Status:** Sold` | `sold` | silent skip |
55	| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` ≥ 7 days old + `**URL:**` present | `refresh-eligible` | yes |
56	| `**Status:** Published` + `**Date:**` < 7 days old | `too-fresh` | yes, action = "too-fresh, skip" |
57	| `**Status:** Published` + no `**URL:**` line | `no-url` | yes, action = "no URL — paste required" |
58	
59	Silent skips are surfaced as a count summary above the candidate table
60	("Silently skipped: N items") so the operator can spot-check that the
61	right things were ignored.
62	
63	### Parser contracts
64	
65	`listing.md`'s canonical format is produced by Folder Mode Phase 4.
66	The Phase R0 classifier uses **strict regex contracts** — anything
67	that does not match is treated as missing rather than guessed at. The
68	worst classification error is a false-positive `refresh-eligible` that
69	deletes a wrong listing, so the parser errs on the side of "skip".
70	
71	| Field | Regex | Source line |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| Status | `^\*\*Status:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**Status:** Published` |
74	| Date | `^\*\*Date:\*\*\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` | `**Date:** 2026-05-21` |
75	| URL | `^\*\*URL:\*\*\s+(\S+)` | `**URL:** https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/...` |
76	| Price | `^\*\*Price:\*\*\s+\$(\d+)` | `**Price:** $140 ono` |
77	| Floor | `Floor:\s*\$(\d+)` | `- Target: ~$130 | Floor: $110 | Garage sale: $70` |
78	
79	Date format is **ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` only.** Anything else means the file
80	was hand-edited and is classified as `not-published` (silent skip).
81	
82	### Proposed-price preview
83	
84	For `refresh-eligible` and `no-url` items, R0 previews the proposed
85	new price using the **default rule** — `−10% clamp-to-floor`, rounded
86	with the seller-rounding rules from the Pricing model. Both R0
87	preview and the Phase R2 final price flow through the same calculator
88	at `scripts/refresh_pricing.py` so the operator sees in R0 exactly
89	what gets posted in R2.
90	
91	If `Floor:` is absent from seller notes, the floor falls back to
92	`list_price × 0.85` (matches Pricing model § 5). The clamp still
93	holds.
94	
95	For `too-fresh` rows, the table shows `—` for proposed price and
96	floor — no decision is being made on these items this session.
97	
98	The floor gate (next section) is where the operator confirms or
99	overrides the previewed price before Phase R1 runs.
100	
101	### Session cap (5 per session)
102	
103	If more than 5 items are `refresh-eligible`:
104	* Sort by age (oldest first).
105	* Take the oldest 5 as the queued set.
106	* Show the rest under `deferred to next session` in the table, with
107	  a count summary in the "### Deferred to next session" section.
108	
109	The cap is FB rate-limit hygiene — bursts >5 refreshes/hour are the
110	shadowban signal in reseller-community data. Re-run the skill after
111	≥30 minutes to drain the deferred set.
112	
113	### Floor gate (the operator-confirmation step)
114	
115	After R0 prints the candidate table and the `no-url` paste pass
116	completes, the skill runs the **floor gate** before handing off to
117	Phase R1. The operator can accept all defaults, override per item, or
118	override in bulk.
119	
120	**Per-item overrides** (one line per item, in any order):
121	
122	| Operator input | Meaning |
123	|---|---|
124	| no response, or item not mentioned | accept the previewed `-10% clamp-to-floor` price |
125	| `<item>: same` | keep the current price (no drop) — useful when comps suggest the price is already right |
126	| `<item>: $X` | set the new price to `$X`, **still clamped to the floor** — operator's number overrides the calculator, the floor stays non-negotiable |
127	
128	**Bulk overrides** (apply to every `refresh-eligible` item in the queued
129	set, not the deferred ones):
130	
131	| Operator input | Meaning |
132	|---|---|
133	| `drop everything N%` | apply `−N%` instead of the default `−10%`, then clamp each item to its own floor |
134	| `keep all prices` | equivalent to `drop everything 0%` — recreate every item at its current price |
135	
136	Resolution order when both kinds of input arrive:
137	
138	1. Apply the bulk rate first (sets the new baseline for every item).
139	2. Apply per-item overrides on top (a per-item `$X` wins over the bulk rate; `same` wins over the bulk rate too).
140	3. Clamp every result to its floor as the last step — the floor is the only invariant the operator cannot override.
141	
142	Operationally the calculator is one function call per item via
143	`scripts/refresh_pricing.py`:
144	
145	```python
146	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.10)   # default
147	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.15)   # "drop everything 15%"
148	proposed_price(current, floor, drop_rate=0.0)    # "same" / "keep all prices"
149	clamp_to_floor(x, floor, current)                # per-item "$X" override
150	```
151	
152	The CLI mirrors the Python API for shell-debug:
153	
154	```bash
155	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 40 --floor 35
156	# 35
157	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_pricing.py --current 100 --floor 80 --drop 0.15
158	# 85
159	```
160	
161	After the floor gate resolves, re-print the queued set as a
162	post-gate confirmation table — same columns, but the `Proposed`
163	column reflects the resolved prices and a new `Drop` column shows
164	the realised percentage (so the operator can spot floor-clamp
165	saves: `$40 → $35 (drop 12.5%, floor)`). The operator confirms once,
166	then Phase R1 begins.
167	
168	### Interaction with the live-price override
169	
170	The live-price override runs **before** the floor gate. It updates
171	the "current price" the calculator sees, in-memory only — `listing.md`
172	is never written back. Sequence:
173	
174	1. R0 classifier reads `**Price:**` from each `listing.md`. This is
175	   the *snapshot at publish time*, not always the live FB price.
176	2. Live-price override prompt: operator pastes `<item>: $X` per
177	   item where the live FB price has drifted from the snapshot.
178	3. Floor gate: defaults and overrides are computed against the
179	   live price from step 2, not the snapshot.
180	
181	This ordering matters: an item published at $50, manually dropped
182	to $35 on FB, with floor $30, should refresh at `max(30, round(35 ×
183	0.9)) = max(30, round(31.5)) = $30` — not at `max(30, round(50 ×
184	0.9)) = $45`, which would be a *price increase*, the opposite of
185	what a refresh is for.
186	
187	### `no-url` interaction
188	
189	When an item is classified `no-url`, the skill prompts the user to
190	paste the listing's FB URL during Phase R0. **The paste is in-memory
191	for the current session only — never written back to `listing.md`.**
192	
193	If the user wants the URL persisted, they need to add the `**URL:**`
194	line manually. A missing URL line in the file is the signal that
195	capture failed at publish time (consistent with the Folder Mode
196	Phase 4 Step 6 rule: omit rather than write a placeholder).
197	
198	### Re-running is identical (no side effects)
199	
200	Phase R0 writes nothing. Re-running on the same folder on the same
201	day, with the same listings, produces the same table. This is the
202	hand-test invariant for the slice.
203	
204	## Output: the candidate table
205	
206	```
207	⚠️  Refresh = delete + relist on FB Marketplace.
208	    DELETE LOSES: saves, chat history, view count.
209	    This is the established tactic for resetting the FB algorithm; the loss is the price.
210	
211	Found 10 items: 5 queued, 1 deferred, 1 no-url, 1 too-fresh, 2 silently skipped (sold or no listing.md).
212	
213	## Candidate table
214	
215	| Item | Age | Current | Proposed | Floor | Action |
216	|------|-----|---------|----------|-------|--------|
217	| eligible-60d | 60d | $50 | $45 | $35 | refresh |
218	| eligible-30d | 30d | $100 | $90 | $70 | refresh |
219	| ...
220	| too-fresh-3d | 3d | $40 | — | — | too-fresh, skip |
221	| eligible-8d | 8d | $25 | $22 | $20 | deferred to next session |
222	
223	### Deferred to next session (1 item)
224	Rate-limit hygiene caps refresh at 5 per session.
225	Re-run `/resell-au refresh ...` after ≥30 minutes to drain the queue.
226	```
227	
228	The data-loss warning prints **exactly once per session** — the start
229	of Phase R0, above the table. Each `/resell-au refresh ...` invocation
230	is one session; subsequent invocations re-print it.
231	
232	## Running the classifier
233	
234	The R0 classifier is implemented as a Python script so the parsing is
235	deterministic and regression-testable. Invoke it directly rather than
236	re-implementing the rules inline — the script is the single source of
237	truth for what counts as `refresh-eligible`.
238	
239	```bash
240	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_r0_classify.py <target_folder>
241	```
242	
243	For deterministic fixture testing, set `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
244	to override the "today" date so age classifications stay stable across
245	runs.
246	
247	## Phase R2 — recreate at new price
248	
249	Phase R2 runs after R1 has confirmed deletion for the current item
250	(`status: deleted` in the run-state JSON, `delete_detection`
251	populated). One item at a time — multi-item batching and resume
252	semantics are documented in § "Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop". The
253	recreate price comes from the R0 floor-gate resolution (default
254	−10% clamp-to-floor, with per-item and bulk overrides) rather than
255	the listing's snapshot.
256	
257	R2 reuses Folder Mode Phase 4 Steps 1–6 verbatim — the recreate
258	form is the same `/marketplace/create/item` flow regardless of
259	whether it's a brand-new listing or a refresh. The only differences
260	are (a) **pre-fill data comes from `listing.md`** rather than from
261	Phase 1 photo-drafted output, and (b) on success, the `listing.md`
262	updater (`scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py`) runs instead of the
263	Phase 4 writer.
264	
265	### Pre-conditions
266	
267	- Phase R1 ran on this item with terminal state `status: deleted`
268	  and `delete_detection ∈ {redirect, listing_gone_copy, row_missing}`.
269	  R2 must NOT run if deletion was unconfirmed
270	  (`delete_detection: "timeout_manual"`) — duplicate-listing risk is
271	  the whole reason R1 stop-the-lines.
272	- Recreate price (`new_price`) is decided by the R0 floor gate.
273	  `old_price` for the refresh-history bullet is the operator-confirmed
274	  live price (live-price override if provided, else `**Price:**`
275	  snapshot from `listing.md`). When the floor gate resolves to the
276	  same value as the live price (e.g. operator typed `same`, or
277	  `−10%` clamped exactly to floor and floor == current), `old_price`
278	  and `new_price` match and the bullet reads `$X → $X`.
279	
280	### Step R2.1 — pre-fill the form payload from listing.md
281	
282	Parse the item's `listing.md` for the recreate inputs:
283	
284	| Phase 4 field | Source line in listing.md |
285	|---|---|
286	| Title | `**Title:**` in `## Ad copy` |
287	| Price | resolved `new_price` from the R0 floor gate (default `proposed_price(current, floor)`, per-item or bulk override applied) |
288	| Category | `**Category:**` in `## Ad copy` |
289	| Condition | `**Condition:**` in `## Ad copy` |
290	| Description | `**Description:**` body in `## Ad copy` |
291	| Location | `**Location:**` in `## Ad copy` |
292	| Photos | every image file in the item's subfolder, in lexical filename order |
293	
294	Photos are not recorded in `listing.md` — they live on disk in the
295	same subfolder Folder Mode Phase 4 originally uploaded from, so a
296	lexical-order listing of `.jpg` / `.jpeg` / `.png` / `.heic` files
297	gives the same photo set. Cap 10 — same as Phase 4.
298	
299	### Step R2.2 — drive the recreate (Phase 4 Steps 1–6)
300	
301	Run `browser-automation.md` § "The loop (one item, one platform)"
302	Steps 1 through 6 verbatim (including Step 6b). The outcome is one of:
303	
304	- `post_publish_detection: "url_match"` — new listing URL captured
305	  directly from the post-publish redirect.
306	- `post_publish_detection: "iframe_extract"` — the publish landed on the
307	  your-listings page or timed out, and Step 6b recovered the real URL from
308	  the Selling-page ad-preview iframe (verified by exact title match).
309	- `post_publish_detection: "your_listings_redirect"` or
310	  `"timeout_manual"` — Publish click landed, but neither the polling loop
311	  nor the Step 6b iframe recovery captured the URL. Ask the operator to
312	  paste it, same flow as Phase 4 Step 6.
313	
314	If the recreate fails at any step (snapshot mismatch, captcha,
315	publish timeout with no URL pasted by the operator):
316	
317	- **Do NOT touch `listing.md`.** Leaving it alone means the next
318	  run sees this item as `no-url` (since no URL was captured) and the
319	  operator can hand-fix or retry — the multi-item loop's resume
320	  contract picks up from this state.
321	- Update the run-state JSON to `status: deleted` (not `recreated`)
322	  and populate `failure_reason` with a short string. The multi-item
323	  loop then surfaces the item as `action: manual` on the next
324	  `plan` call.
325	
326	### Step R2.3 — update listing.md
327	
328	When a new URL is available (from `url_match`, `iframe_extract`, or
329	operator paste), run the updater:
330	
331	```bash
332	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_listing_md_update.py \
333	    <item_subfolder>/listing.md \
334	    --old-url   "<old URL from run-state>" \
335	    --new-url   "<new URL>" \
336	    --age-days  <age_days from run-state> \
337	    --old-price <old_price from run-state> \
338	    --new-price <new_price from run-state>
339	```
340	
341	`old_price` is the live-confirmed price the listing was running at
342	before the refresh; `new_price` is the floor-gate-resolved price the
343	recreate posted at. They differ when the drop took effect (typical
344	case) and match when the operator chose `same` or the floor clamp
345	caught a drop that would have been smaller than the rounding band.
346	
347	The script (deterministic, byte-identical on Comps):
348	
349	- Replaces `**URL:**` with the new URL (inserts the line after
350	  `**Platform:**` if absent — the `no-url` paste-in-R0 case).
351	- Replaces `**Date:**` with today (`REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`
352	  overrides for deterministic tests).
353	- Leaves `**Price:**` byte-identical.
354	- Creates or appends `## Refresh history` between `## Seller notes`
355	  and `## Comps`, adding one bullet:
356	  ```
357	  - YYYY-MM-DD (refresh #N): $X → $Y. Old URL: <old>. New URL: <new>. Age at refresh: Nd.
358	  ```
359	  The refresh number increments from any existing `(refresh #N)`
360	  bullet in the section.
361	- Refuses to write if the `## Comps` block (heading to end-of-file)
362	  is not byte-identical — internal safety guard against the
363	  refresh history insertion accidentally clobbering captured comp
364	  data.
365	
366	Pass `--dry-run` to print to stdout instead of mutating the file
367	(used by the regression tests in `tests/check_refresh_r2.sh`).
368	
369	### Step R2.4 — finalise run-state
370	
371	On successful update:
372	
373	```
374	status: recreated
375	new_url: <captured URL>
376	```
377	
378	`delete_detection` was already populated by R1 and is carried
379	forward unchanged.
380	
381	## Phase R1+R2 multi-item loop
382	
383	After R0 produces the queued set (up to 5 items, oldest-first) and
384	the operator confirms the floor gate, the skill runs R1 then R2 for
385	each queued item in order, with **30–90 s human-cadence delays**
386	between items. The loop is driven off the Refresh Mode run-state
387	JSON file, which is **the single source of truth** for what each
388	item's next action is — both for the in-session loop and for
389	resuming after a crash, `/compact`, or the user killing the session.
390	
391	The orchestration script is `scripts/refresh_runstate.py`. It has
392	three subcommands; the agent's loop is built on `init` (start or
393	resume), `plan` (what's next), `update` (record the result).
394	
395	### Step M0 — init or resume the run-state file
396	
397	After the floor gate, build a queued items array and pass it to
398	`init`. The script's behaviour is the resume contract:
399	
400	```bash
401	# JSON file with one object per queued item — see schema below.
402	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py init <target_folder> \
403	    --queued-json /tmp/queued.json
404	```
405	
406	| Folder state | What init does |
407	|---|---|
408	| No `.resell-au-refresh-*.json` in folder | Create a new file `<folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json` seeded from `--queued-json`. Print its path. |
409	| Latest file has any item in `pending`, `deleted`, or `failed` | **Resume** — print the existing file's path, ignore `--queued-json`. This is the load-bearing rule for the "kill mid-flight + restart" path. |
410	| Latest file has all items in `recreated` / `skipped` | Treat as new run — create a new file from `--queued-json`. (The drained-queue-then-add-more case.) |
411	| Latest file unreadable (JSON corrupted) | Exit non-zero. Do not silently overwrite — the operator may want to recover it. |
412	
413	**The same run-state file is updated in place across resumes.** A
414	restart never produces a new timestamped file — `init` returns the
415	existing path, the loop continues mutating it.
416	
417	The queued-item JSON shape (the agent assembles this from R0's
418	classified set + the floor-gate-resolved prices, then feeds it to
419	init):
420	
421	```json
422	[
423	  {
424	    "subfolder": "kettlebell",
425	    "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
426	    "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
427	    "old_price": 45,
428	    "new_price": 40,
429	    "floor": 35,
430	    "age_days": 12,
431	    "refresh_count_before": 0
432	  }
433	]
434	```
435	
436	`refresh_count_before` is optional (defaults to 0) and informational
437	only — the listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number
438	from existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file, so this
439	field doesn't need to be accurate.
440	
441	### Step M1 — defer-notice before R1 starts
442	
443	Before the first R1 begins, print the defer notice **exactly once**
444	per session, naming the deferred items so the operator knows what
445	will be left over. R0 already shows the deferred set in the
446	candidate table; this is the "confirming what I'm about to do"
447	message at the start of execution:
448	
449	```
450	Processing 5 items this session. Deferred to next session
451	(≥30 min from now): eligible-8d, eligible-9d.
452	Re-run `/resell-au refresh <folder>` after the cooldown to drain them.
453	```
454	
455	If zero items are deferred, skip the message entirely — no value
456	in noise.
457	
458	### Step M2 — loop on `plan` until no `r1`/`r2` actions remain
459	
460	Each iteration calls `plan`, which emits one JSON object per item
461	(newline-delimited) with a `status` and a derived `action`:
462	
463	```bash
464	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py plan <runstate_path>
465	```
466	
467	| `status` in run-state | `action` from plan | Loop branches to |
468	|---|---|---|
469	| `pending` | `r1` | R1 delete loop in `browser-automation.md` → on success, `update --status deleted`; on confirmed deletion failure, `update --status failed` |
470	| `deleted` | `r2` | R2 recreate (§ "Phase R2 — recreate at new price" above) — **do NOT re-run R1**, the old listing is already gone (would 404) |
471	| `recreated` | `done` | Skip — item already finished in this run-state |
472	| `skipped` | `done` | Skip — operator-decided terminal |
473	| `failed` | `manual` | Surface the item + `failure_reason` to the operator; do not auto-retry. Operator can edit the run-state file by hand or re-run R0 once the underlying issue is fixed. |
474	
475	Take the first item whose action is `r1` or `r2`, run that phase,
476	update the run-state, then sleep 30–90 s (random) using
477	`run_in_background: true` on a Bash `sleep` — same pattern as Phase
478	4 Step 7 / R1.8. After the sleep, re-run `plan` and continue.
479	The loop terminates when no items have action `r1` or `r2` left.
480	
481	The per-item delay applies between **items**, not between R1 and R2
482	of the same item — R1 hands directly to R2 once deletion is
483	confirmed, with no inter-phase delay (per the Phase R2 pre-condition
484	that the delete confirmation be recent and unambiguous).
485	
486	### Step M3 — update after each phase
487	
488	After a phase resolves, write the result back:
489	
490	```bash
491	# Successful deletion.
492	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
493	    --item 0 --status deleted --delete-detection redirect
494	
495	# Successful recreate.
496	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
497	    --item 0 --status recreated --new-url "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/"
498	
499	# Confirmed failure (e.g. deletion timeout, operator picked "continue" to skip).
500	python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_runstate.py update <runstate_path> \
501	    --item 0 --status failed --failure-reason "delete timeout — operator skipped"
502	```
503	
504	`update` is atomic (temp + rename) so a kill mid-write can't
505	corrupt the file. The corresponding `*_at` field
506	(`pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
507	`failed_at`) is auto-stamped on every status transition —
508	`pending_at` is stamped by `init` at creation time. The
509	timestamps let the operator verify the 30–90 s inter-item gap
510	from the file alone, no shell history needed.
511	
512	### Resume in practice
513	
514	Headline scenario: kill the run after item 0 is `deleted` but before
515	`recreated`, re-invoke `/resell-au refresh <folder>`. The skill then:
516	
517	1. Calls `init <folder>` (no `--queued-json` needed) — picks up
518	   the existing `.resell-au-refresh-…json`.
519	2. Calls `plan` — item 0 has `action: r2` (resume from recreate;
520	   the old listing is already gone), items 1+ have `action: r1`.
521	3. Runs R2 for item 0 first (no R1 re-run, no 404 risk), then
522	   R1+R2 for the rest, with 30–90 s gaps between items.
523	4. The same run-state file ends up with every item at `recreated`
524	   — **never a new file per resume**.
525	
526	## Refresh Mode run-state file
527	
528	Written to `<target_folder>/.resell-au-refresh-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json`
529	by `scripts/refresh_runstate.py init` at the start of the R1+R2
530	loop. Refresh runs use a separate file from Folder Mode runs because
531	the per-item shape differs (no comp block, no platforms map —
532	refresh is single-platform, single-action).
533	
534	```json
535	{
536	  "run_started": "ISO 8601 timestamp",
537	  "target_folder": "/path/to/folder",
538	  "session_cap": 5,
539	  "items": [
540	    {
541	      "subfolder": "kettlebell",
542	      "title": "12kg Kettlebell — like new",
543	      "old_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/111/",
544	      "old_price": 45,
545	      "new_price": 40,
546	      "floor": 35,
547	      "age_days": 12,
548	      "refresh_count_before": 0,
549	      "status": "pending | deleted | recreated | failed | skipped",
550	      "delete_detection": "redirect | listing_gone_copy | row_missing | timeout_manual | null",
551	      "new_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ | null",
552	      "failure_reason": "string | null",
553	      "pending_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
554	      "deleted_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
555	      "recreated_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
556	      "skipped_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
557	      "failed_at": "ISO 8601 | null"
558	    }
559	  ]
560	}
561	```
562	
563	Resume semantics:
564	
565	| Terminal state | Meaning |
566	|---|---|
567	| `pending` | Not started — R1 has not yet deleted. Resume from R1. |
568	| `deleted` | R1 succeeded but R2 did not capture a new URL. Resume from R2 — the OLD listing is already gone. Do not re-run R1 (would 404). |
569	| `recreated` | R2 succeeded, `listing.md` updated. Item is done. |
570	| `skipped` | Operator-decided skip (e.g. unrecoverable mismatch). Do not retry. |
571	| `failed` | Phase failed and operator has not yet decided next step. Re-running `init` will resume the file; `plan` surfaces these as `action: manual` so the operator chooses (edit run-state by hand, or fix the underlying issue and re-run). |
572	
573	The `pending_at` / `deleted_at` / `recreated_at` / `skipped_at` /
574	`failed_at` fields are auto-stamped by
575	`scripts/refresh_runstate.py` — `pending_at` at `init` time,
576	the rest on each `update` call. The inter-item-delay
577	verification (each item-to-item gap between 30 and 90 s) works
578	off the file alone — no shell history needed.
579	
580	`session_cap` is written into the run-state at `init` for
581	observability (it tells anyone inspecting the file "this run was
582	capped at 5"). The cap is enforced in two places: upstream in
583	`refresh_r0_classify.py` (trims eligible items to `SESSION_CAP`
584	before writing `--queued-json`), and defensively in
585	`refresh_runstate.py init` (refuses `--queued-json` arrays longer
586	than `SESSION_CAP` with a non-zero exit). The double enforcement
587	guards against an R0 regression silently passing too many items to
588	the loop. `refresh_count_before` is similarly informational; the
589	listing.md updater derives the canonical refresh number from
590	existing `## Refresh history` bullets in the file rather than
591	trusting this field.
592	
593	## Phase R3 — summary output
594	
595	After the multi-item loop drains (every queued item has terminal
596	status `recreated` / `failed` / `skipped`), Phase R3 reads the
597	run-state JSON and prints one summary block to the user. R3 is
598	read-only: no further `listing.md` updates, no browser actions.
599	
600	### Output format
601	
602	```
603	## Refresh summary
604	
605	5 items processed: 4 refreshed, 0 skipped, 1 failed.
606	
607	| Item | Status | Detail |
608	|------|--------|--------|
609	| kettlebell | refreshed | $45 → $40 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/222/ (was 111) |
610	| ikea-rugs  | refreshed | $40 → $35 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/444/ (was 333) |
611	| violin     | refreshed | $100 → $90 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/666/ (was 555) |
612	| bookshelf  | refreshed | $80 → $72 — https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/888/ (was 777) |
613	| chair      | failed    | delete timeout — operator skipped |
614	
615	Deferred to next session (2 items, re-run after ≥30 min):
616	- couch (10d)
617	- mirror (8d)
618	```
619	
620	### Per-row composition
621	
622	| Run-state `status` | Row "Status" | Row "Detail" |
623	|---|---|---|
624	| `recreated` | `refreshed` | `$<old_price> → $<new_price> — <new_url> (was <old_id>)` where `<old_id>` is the digits in `old_url` between `/marketplace/item/` and the trailing `/` |
625	| `skipped` | `skipped` | `failure_reason` verbatim (operator-typed at the stop-the-line `continue` prompt) |
626	| `failed` | `failed` | `failure_reason` verbatim |
627	| `pending` / `deleted` | — | should not appear at R3 — loop only exits on terminal states. If present, the loop terminated abnormally; surface a stop-the-line message instead of the summary table |
628	
629	### Deferred section
630	
631	The R0-classified items that were over the 5-per-session cap are not
632	in the run-state JSON (only the queued 5 are). R3 sources them from
633	the R0 classifier output retained in memory for the session. Format
634	is `<subfolder> (<age_days>d)` per line, sorted oldest-first to
635	match R0's queueing order.
636	
637	If zero items were deferred, **omit the entire `Deferred to next
638	session` section** — no value in printing empty noise.
639	
640	### Total processed count
641	
642	Header counts come from the run-state items array — total = items in
643	the run-state (not including R0-deferred items). The sum of
644	refreshed + skipped + failed equals total processed.
645	
646	## Tests and fixtures
647	
648	All scripts ship with deterministic fixtures or unit tests so the
649	contracts above are regression-checked. Run after touching the
650	matching script.
651	
652	| Script | Tests | Invocation | Env override |
653	|---|---|---|---|
654	| `refresh_r0_classify.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r0/` (golden diff covering all 5 buckets + cap deferral) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r0.sh` | `REFRESH_R0_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
655	| `refresh_listing_md_update.py` | `tests/fixtures/refresh-r2/` (3 cases: first-refresh-with-comps, second-refresh, no-url-no-comps) | `bash tests/check_refresh_r2.sh` | `REFRESH_R2_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD` |
656	| `refresh_pricing.py` | `tests/test_refresh_pricing.py` (unittest: acceptance cases, per-item + bulk overrides, rounding bands, absent-floor fallback) | `bash tests/check_refresh_pricing.sh` | — |
657	| `refresh_runstate.py` | `tests/test_refresh_runstate.py` (unittest: status-action mapping, `*_at` auto-stamp, find-latest, filename format, init CLI integration) | `bash tests/check_refresh_runstate.sh` | `REFRESH_RUNSTATE_NOW=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` |
658	
659	The fixtures are parser-correctness only. End-to-end verification —
660	the real eval — is a hand-run against `~/Desktop/things-for-sale/`
661	with the candidate table and summary table sanity-checked against
662	what the operator expects.
663	
```
