1	# Browser Automation Loop
2	
3	The agent runs this loop in Folder Mode Phase 4 for each item × platform pair.
4	It is the generic orchestration layer; platform-specific field maps live in
5	`facebook-marketplace.md`.
6	
7	## Pre-conditions (verified in Phase 0 before this loop ever runs)
8	
9	- Chrome is reachable on port 9222.
10	- User is logged in to Facebook Marketplace in the attached Chrome.
11	- All items have been drafted, priced, and ad copy approved (Phases 1–3).
12	
13	The same Chrome session is also used in **Phase 2** for FB Marketplace
14	comp search (Layer 2 in `live-comp-search.md`). A Marketplace search tab may
15	remain open from Phase 2 when Phase 4 begins — leave it alone; Phase 4
16	navigates a separate tab to the create-listing URL.
17	
18	## The loop (one item, one platform)
19	
20	### Step 1 — Navigate
21	
22	Navigate to the create-listing URL:
23	
24	- Facebook Marketplace: `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/create/item`
25	
26	Wait for the page to fully load before snapshotting (use `wait_for` on a
27	known stable element — see the platform-specific file for the selector).
28	
29	### Step 2 — Snapshot
30	
31	Call `take_snapshot` to get the accessibility tree. This is the source of
32	truth for all subsequent interaction. Never rely on remembered CSS selectors
33	or XPaths from prior runs — DOM layouts change quarterly.
34	
35	**If the snapshot doesn't match the field map in the platform reference file:**
36	
37	1. Stop immediately.
38	2. Take a screenshot with `take_screenshot`.
39	3. Show the user the screenshot and the field map you expected.
40	4. Ask: *"The [Platform] listing form has changed layout. Can you confirm what
41	   the [field name] field looks like now? I'll update my reference before
42	   continuing."*
43	5. Do not guess. Do not click elements that "look similar". Wait for the user
44	   to confirm before proceeding.
45	
46	### Step 3 — Fill fields
47	
48	Fill fields in the order the platform form expects them. Use element UIDs from
49	the accessibility snapshot, not CSS selectors. After filling each field,
50	re-snapshot to confirm the value was accepted (some fields trigger dynamic
51	updates — category selection is the most common).
52	
53	Fill order:
54	
55	- **Facebook Marketplace**: photos → category → title → price → condition →
56	  description → location → hide-from-friends toggle. See
57	  `facebook-marketplace.md` for the exact interaction sequence.
58	
59	### Step 4 — Upload photos
60	
61	Use the platform's file-upload element UID from the snapshot. Upload in
62	**lexical filename order** — the first file becomes the lead photo.
63	
64	Upload protocol:
65	
66	1. Call `upload_file` with the element UID and the first photo path.
67	2. Snapshot. Confirm the thumbnail appeared. If it didn't, wait 2 s and
68	   snapshot again. If it still hasn't appeared after two checks, stop and
69	   tell the user.
70	3. Repeat for each photo. Cap at 10 — do not attempt an 11th upload.
71	
72	Do not upload all photos in one call even if the MCP supports it — confirm
73	each thumbnail before the next upload.
74	
75	### Step 5 — Review screen — verify then publish
76	
77	After all fields are filled and photos uploaded, the form presents a review /
78	preview screen before final submission.
79	
80	1. Snapshot the review screen.
81	2. Take a `take_screenshot`.
82	3. **Verify** title, price, condition, and description all match the approved
83	   ad copy. Check each field explicitly against the Phase 3 approved block.
84	4. If any field looks wrong: fix it (navigate back or use inline edit on the
85	   review screen), re-snapshot to confirm, then return to step 1.
86	5. If everything is correct: locate the Publish / Post button in the snapshot
87	   and click it.
88	
89	### Step 6 — Confirm the listing is live
90	
91	After clicking Publish, **do not use `wait_for` to detect navigation** — that
92	MCP tool matches page text content, not URL changes, and will never resolve
93	on the post-publish redirect. Instead, poll the URL via `evaluate_script`.
94	
95	**Detection protocol** — Facebook Marketplace:
96	
97	1. Poll `window.location.href` every **500 ms** for up to **15 s** using
98	   `evaluate_script` with body `return window.location.href;`.
99	
100	2. **Success path A — listing URL matched.** URL matches
101	   `^https://www\.facebook\.com/marketplace/item/\d+/?(\?.*)?$`:
102	   - Capture the full URL.
103	   - Record `{ status: "posted", post_publish_detection: "url_match",
104	     listing_url: "<captured>", timestamp }` in the run-state JSON.
105	   - Write the URL to `listing.md` under the `**URL:**` field.
106	   - Break the poll. Tell the user: *"Posted `<item>` — `<URL>`."*
107	
108	3. **Success path B — redirect to your-listings.** URL matches
109	   `/marketplace/you/selling` or `/marketplace/your_listings` (FB A/B tests
110	   this destination):
111	   - Record `{ status: "posted", post_publish_detection:
112	     "your_listings_redirect", listing_url: null }` in the run-state
113	     (provisional).
114	   - Break the poll and go to **Step 6b** to attempt automatic URL recovery
115	     before involving the operator.
116	
117	4. **Timeout — 15 s elapsed without a match.**
118	   - Record `{ status: "posted", post_publish_detection: "timeout_manual",
119	     listing_url: null }` in the run-state (provisional — user will confirm).
120	   - Go to **Step 6b** to attempt automatic URL recovery before involving the
121	     operator. Do not retry-click Publish.
122	
123	5. If at any point during the poll the page shows an error banner, a captcha,
124	   or a "posting too fast" warning: **stop immediately**. Screenshot + surface
125	   to user per the stop-the-line conditions below.
126	
127	**Why polling, not `wait_for`:** `wait_for` waits for text to appear on the
128	page. The post-publish state is a URL change, not a text change — there is no
129	reliable text token to wait for. A 500 ms `evaluate_script` poll is the
130	correct shape, and 30 calls over 15 s is trivial load on CDP.
131	
132	### Step 6b — Recover URL from Selling-page iframe
133	
134	Reached only from Step 6 Path B (`your_listings_redirect`) or the 15 s
135	timeout (`timeout_manual`) — the listing went live but the poll never saw a
136	`/marketplace/item/<id>/` URL. The real URL can usually still be recovered
137	from the ad-preview iframe FB renders on the filtered Selling page, so try
138	that before bothering the operator. (On Path A, Step 6 has already captured
139	the URL and broken the poll — Step 6b never runs.)
140	
141	1. **Navigate** the tab to the title-filtered Selling page:
142	   `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/you/selling?title_search=<URL-encoded title>`,
143	   where `<title>` is the title just published (the Phase 3 approved
144	   `**Title:**`).
145	
146	2. **Poll for the iframe** for up to ~5 s (`evaluate_script` every 500 ms),
147	   waiting for `iframe[src*="ads/ad_preview_generator_iframe"]` to appear on
148	   the parent DOM. No `take_snapshot` is needed — the iframe `src` is on the
149	   parent page and readable via `evaluate_script` alone.
150	
151	3. **Extract** the URL and name with this `evaluate_script` body:
152	
153	   ```js
154	   () => {
155	     const f = document.querySelector('iframe[src*="ads/ad_preview_generator_iframe"]');
156	     if (!f || !f.src) return null;
157	     const m = f.src.match(/[?&]creative_spec=([^&]+)/);
158	     if (!m) return null;
159	     try {
160	       const spec = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(m[1]));
161	       const ld = spec.object_story_spec.link_data;
162	       if (!ld || typeof ld.link !== 'string' || typeof ld.name !== 'string') return null;
163	       return { url: ld.link, name: ld.name };
164	     } catch (e) {
165	       return null;
166	     }
167	   }
168	   ```
169	
170	   `link_data.link` is the real `/marketplace/item/<id>/` URL; `link_data.name`
171	   is the listing title, used below to confirm identity.
172	
173	4. **Identity check.** Compare the returned `name` against the title just
174	   published — an exact match after trimming surrounding whitespace on both
175	   sides. Do not loosen beyond a trim; substring or fuzzy matching reopens the
176	   wrong-attribution risk. **Match** →
177	   - Record `{ status: "posted", post_publish_detection: "iframe_extract",
178	     listing_url: "<url>" }` in the run-state, overwriting the provisional
179	     `your_listings_redirect` / `timeout_manual` key.
180	   - Write the URL to `listing.md` under `**URL:**` (Step 7).
181	   - Tell the user: *"Posted `<item>` — recovered URL from Selling page:
182	     `<URL>`."*
183	   - Done. Skip the paste fallback below.
184	
185	5. **Mismatch or extraction failure** — the extractor returns `null`, the
186	   `name` doesn't match the published title exactly, or the iframe never
187	   appeared within ~5 s. Fall through to the operator-paste fallback, keeping
188	   the provisional key already recorded (`your_listings_redirect` or
189	   `timeout_manual` — do not change it):
190	   - `take_screenshot`.
191	   - For `your_listings_redirect`: *"Posted `<item>` — FB redirected to the
192	     your-listings page and I couldn't auto-recover the URL. Paste it here if
193	     you want it stored in `listing.md`."*
194	   - For `timeout_manual`: *"Publish click sent, but I couldn't confirm the
195	     listing went live within 15 s and couldn't auto-recover the URL.
196	     Screenshot attached. Was it published? If yes, paste the listing URL."*
197	   - Wait for the operator's reply before continuing to Step 7. Do not
198	     retry-click Publish.
199	
200	**Why the `name` check matters:** with two listings published in quick
201	succession, the filtered Selling page may surface the wrong row's iframe
202	first. The exact-title match is what stops a recovered URL being attributed
203	to the wrong item — on any doubt, fall through to paste rather than guess.
204	
205	### Step 7 — Human-cadence delay
206	
207	After each successfully handled listing (whether posted or skipped), pause
208	**30–90 seconds (random)** before starting the next item.
209	
210	Tell the user: *"Waiting [N] s before the next listing…"*
211	
212	Never skip these delays. Burst posting is the primary detection trigger.
213	
214	**How to actually pause** — the Claude Code Bash tool blocks long leading
215	`sleep` commands (the harness rejects `sleep 60` and similar). Use one of:
216	
217	1. **`run_in_background: true`** on a `sleep N` Bash call — the harness
218	   accepts it, the task ID is returned immediately, and you get a completion
219	   notification when it finishes. This is the cleanest pattern.
220	2. **Bash `Monitor` with an until-loop** for conditional waits — e.g.
221	   `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`. Only when polling external state.
222	
223	Do not chain shorter `sleep` calls to work around the block — the harness
224	detects that pattern. Do not poll with multiple Bash calls in a loop —
225	`run_in_background` already gives you a single notification.
226

228	
229	## Refresh Mode — Phase R1 delete loop (one item)
230	
231	Phase R1 runs after R0 produces a confirmed queued set. It deletes
232	ONE already-published listing on FB Marketplace, then verifies
233	deletion. **Recreate (Phase R2) does not run in this phase** —
234	duplicate-listing risk is bounded by completing the delete and
235	confirming it before handing back.
236	
237	Locator patterns are in `facebook-marketplace.md` § "Delete listing
238	locators (Refresh Mode Phase R1)". This section is the orchestration
239	sequence — read both before running.
240	
241	R1 is one step in the **multi-item R1+R2 loop** orchestrated by
242	`scripts/refresh_runstate.py`. The loop decides which item runs
243	next (and whether the next action for that item is R1 or R2 —
244	resume can start from R2 when R1 has already deleted the listing
245	in a prior session). Read `refresh-strategy.md` § "Phase R1+R2
246	multi-item loop" for the loop structure, the defer notice that
247	precedes the first R1, and the resume contract; this section
248	documents the per-item R1 mechanics.
249	
250	### Pre-conditions
251	
252	- Phase R0 has classified the target as `refresh-eligible` and the
253	  user has confirmed the queued set.
254	- The item's `listing.md` has a `**URL:**` line (the post-deletion
255	  poll target) AND a `**Title:**` line (the selling-page filter
256	  input).
257	- Chrome attached on port 9222, FB Marketplace logged in (Phase 0
258	  pre-flight already passed).
259	
260	### Step R1.1 — Navigate to the seller's filtered listings page
261	
262	The delete affordance lives only on `/marketplace/you/selling/`, not
263	on the listing detail page. Navigate using the title filter param so
264	the target row loads in the first batch:
265	
266	```
267	https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/you/selling?title_search=<URL-encoded title>
268	```
269	
270	The title comes from the `**Title:**` line in the item's `listing.md`
271	(produced by Folder Mode Phase 4 Step 7). URL-encode it before
272	appending — titles routinely contain spaces, `&`, `+`, hyphens, and
273	the `~` character.
274	
275	### Step R1.2 — Snapshot, verify the target row exists
276	
277	Call `take_snapshot`. Find a `button "More options for <Title>"` whose
278	accessible name matches the expected title exactly.
279	
280	**Verification gate:** If zero matching rows exist, the listing is
281	already deleted (rare but possible — e.g. previous interrupted run).
282	Mark the item `status: deleted, delete_detection: "row_missing"` in
283	the run-state JSON and skip to Step R1.7 to confirm via URL poll.
284	
285	If more than one row matches (rare — listing duplicated): disambiguate
286	by `target_id=<listing_id>` in the row's `Promote now` link URL. The
287	listing_id is the digits in the stored `**URL:**` between
288	`/marketplace/item/` and the trailing `/`.
289	
290	### Step R1.3 — Open the "More options" menu
291	
292	Snapshot. Click the `"More options for <Title>"` button. Re-snapshot.
293	
294	The opened menu has role `menu "More options for listing"` with these
295	items (order may vary):
296	
297	```
298	menuitem "Renew (N days)"   // disabled until 7-day cooldown elapses
299	menuitem "Mark as pending"
300	menuitem "View listing"
301	menuitem "List in more places"
302	menuitem "Edit listing"
303	menuitem "Delete listing"
304	menuitem "View messages"
305	```
306	
307	If the menu doesn't open (snapshot still shows `expandable` collapsed),
308	re-click once. If still closed: **stop the line** — show user, do not
309	proceed.
310	
311	### Step R1.4 — Click "Delete listing"
312	
313	Re-snapshot. Click `menuitem "Delete listing"`. Re-snapshot.
314	
315	A modal opens: `dialog "Delete listing"` containing a confirm heading
316	and the listing's title + price as static text.
317	
318	### Step R1.5 — Verify listing identity, then click Delete
319	
320	**Read the modal's title + price text. Compare against the expected
321	item from the run-state JSON.** If they don't match — stop the line.
322	This is the last point at which the wrong listing can be aborted.
323	
324	If they match: click `button "Delete"` inside the modal.
325	
326	### Step R1.6 — Handle the "Did you sell this item?" follow-up
327	
328	After the first Delete click, FB shows a second-stage screen:
329	`heading "Did you sell this item?"` with four radio options. Defaults
330	to no selection; `button "Next"` is disabled until one is picked.
331	
332	**Choose `radio "No, haven't sold"`** — that is the truthful answer
333	for refresh-mode (we are delisting due to staleness, not due to a
334	sale). Picking "Yes, sold …" might signal to FB's algorithm that the
335	item is no longer available, which is the opposite of what we want
336	when we relist it minutes later.
337	
338	Click the radio, re-snapshot to confirm `checked`, then click
339	`button "Next"`. The modal closes. The row disappears from the
340	filtered Selling page.
341	
342	### Step R1.7 — Verify deletion (poll the OLD listing URL)
343	
344	Navigate the same tab to the stored `**URL:**` from `listing.md`
345	(`https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/<id>/`). Then poll
346	`window.location.href` via `evaluate_script` every **500 ms for up to
347	15 s**, same shape as Phase 4 Step 6:
348	
349	```javascript
350	() => ({ url: window.location.href,
351	         hasGoneCopy: document.body.innerText.toLowerCase()
352	                       .includes("no longer available") ||
353	                       document.body.innerText.toLowerCase()
354	                       .includes("isn't available") })
355	```
356	
357	Three outcomes:
358	
359	1. **Success path A — URL redirect.** `window.location.href` no
360	   longer matches the original `^/marketplace/item/\d+/?$` pattern.
361	   The observed redirect is `…/marketplace/melbourne/?unavailable_product=1`
362	   — the `unavailable_product=1` query param is the cleanest single
363	   test. Record `delete_detection: "redirect", status: "deleted"`.
364	
365	2. **Success path B — listing-gone copy.** Page text contains
366	   "no longer available" or "isn't available". Record
367	   `delete_detection: "listing_gone_copy", status: "deleted"`. (Both
368	   signals typically fire together; either alone is sufficient.)
369	
370	3. **Timeout — 15 s without either signal.** Stop the line. Take a
371	   screenshot. Record `delete_detection: "timeout_manual",
372	   status: "delete_unconfirmed"`. **Do NOT proceed to Phase R2 (or to
373	   any other item)** — re-listing while the old listing might still
374	   be live duplicates content and is a primary trigger for FB's
375	   content-similarity flag. Surface to user:
376	   *"Couldn't confirm deletion of `<item>` within 15 s. Screenshot
377	   attached. Please verify the listing is gone in the browser and
378	   reply `continue` (skip recreate) or `manual-delete` (delete it
379	   yourself, then I'll continue)."*
380	
381	### Step R1.8 — Human-cadence delay before next item
382	
383	Same protocol as Phase 4 Step 7 — **30–90 s random pause** before
384	moving to the next item's R1 sequence. Use Bash `run_in_background:
385	true` on `sleep N`; do not skip.
386	
387	The delay runs at the **multi-item loop level**, not after every
388	phase. R1 hands directly to R2 for the same item (no inter-phase
389	sleep — see `refresh-strategy.md` § "Step M2"), then the sleep
390	fires before the loop picks up the next item's R1.
391	
392	The session cap of 5 deletes per session (Refresh Mode hygiene rule)
393	caps the burst risk even with the inter-item delay. Over-cap items
394	defer to a future session ≥30 min later; the defer notice listing
395	them by name prints once at the start of the loop (see
396	`refresh-strategy.md` § "Step M1").
397	
398	---
399	
400	## Stop-the-line conditions
401	
402	These apply to both **Phase 4 listing creation** (the loop above) and
403	**Phase 2 comp search** (Layers 1–2 in `live-comp-search.md` — both are now
404	browser-driven). Stop the loop immediately and surface the issue to the user
405	if:
406	
407	| Condition | Action |
408	|---|---|
409	| Captcha / hCaptcha appears | Screenshot + "Captcha appeared — please solve it in the browser, then reply `continue`." Do not attempt to solve it. |
410	| 2FA prompt appears | Screenshot + "2FA required — please complete it in the browser, then reply `continue`." |
411	| "Posting too fast" / rate-limit message | Screenshot + "Rate-limit warning on [Platform]. Suggest waiting at least 10 minutes before continuing. Reply `continue` when ready." |
412	| Login wall (session expired) | Screenshot + "Logged out of [Platform]. Please log back in in the browser, then reply `continue`." |
413	| eBay bot block persists (Layer 1: "Access Denied" or `splashui/challenge` still showing after ~8 s + one reload) | Not the transient ~3 s challenge, which clears itself — only a block that won't clear. For a single item: record `skipped_reason: "stop_the_line"` on `ebay_sold` and lean on Layers 2–3 (read-only search — don't halt the whole run). If it blocks across several items in a row, that's an IP rate-limit → stop the line and surface, as for the rate-limit row above. |
414	| Snapshot doesn't match field map | As described in Step 2 above. |
415	| MCP error / navigation failure | Surface the error, stop. Do not retry silently. |
416	| **Undetected deletion** (Phase R1 only) | After the 15 s URL poll, if neither `unavailable_product=1` redirect nor "no longer available" copy is observed: screenshot + "Couldn't confirm deletion of `<item>` within 15 s. Do NOT proceed to recreate. Please verify in the browser, then reply `continue` (skip the recreate for this item) or `manual-delete` (you'll delete it manually first)." Never re-list while deletion is unconfirmed. |
417	| **Listing identity mismatch in delete-confirm modal** (Phase R1 only) | Title or price shown in the `dialog "Delete listing"` modal does not match the run-state JSON for this item: stop, screenshot, do not click Delete. Surface to user. |
418	
419	On `continue` reply: re-snapshot the current state and resume from Step 2.
420

422	
423	## Run-state file
424	
425	Written to `<target_folder>/.resell-au-run-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.json`.
426	
427	Schema:
428	
429	```json
430	{
431	  "run_started": "ISO 8601 timestamp",
432	  "target_folder": "/path/to/folder",
433	  "items": [
434	    {
435	      "subfolder": "item-name",
436	      "title": "Ad title",
437	      "list_price": 140,
438	      "floor": 110,
439	      "garage_sale": 70,
440	      "ad_copy": "Full description text",
441	      "photos": ["photo1.jpg", "photo2.jpg"],
442	      "comps": {
443	        "captured_at": "ISO 8601",
444	        "confidence": "high | medium | low",
445	        "anchor_source": "sold_median | blended | asking_only",
446	        "ebay_sold":      { "median": 72, "min": 55, "max": 110, "count": 8, "window_days": 60, "search_url": "...", "skipped_reason": null },
447	        "fb_marketplace": { "median": 95, "min": 80, "max": 140, "count": 6, "query": "...", "skipped_reason": null },
448	        "google_fallback": { "ran": false, "notes": null }
449	      },
450	      "platforms": {
451	        "facebook_marketplace": "posted | skipped | failed | pending"
452	      },
453	      "post_publish_detection": "url_match | iframe_extract | your_listings_redirect | timeout_manual | null",
454	      "listing_url": "https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/<id>/ | null"
455	    }
456	  ]
457	}
458	```
459	
460	The `comps` block is populated in **Phase 2** before Phase 4 ever runs. Every
461	sub-source key is present even when its layer was skipped — `skipped_reason`
462	records why. Full layer-source semantics and run-budget rules live in
463	`live-comp-search.md`.
464	
465	Write the file after Phase 3 (with all items at `pending`), then update each
466	item's platform status as you go. This means an interrupted run can be resumed
467	by reading the file and skipping already-posted items.
468	
469	---
470	
471	## Common rationalisations to reject
472	
473	| Rationalisation | Why it fails |
474	|---|---|
475	| "The element UID looks similar to what I'd expect — I'll just click it." | DOM layouts change. A wrong click can trigger actions that are hard to undo (e.g. posting to the wrong category, submitting a draft prematurely). Always re-snapshot and verify. |
476	| "I'll try to solve the captcha automatically." | Automated captcha solving is exactly the behaviour that triggers bans. Stop the line, hand to user. |
477	| "I'll skip the delay — we're in a hurry." | The delay is ban-avoidance, not convenience. Skipping it is the primary detection trigger. |
478	| "The review screen fields look roughly right — I'll just publish." | Verify each field explicitly against the approved copy before clicking Publish. "Roughly right" is how wrong content gets posted. |
479	
```

```json
{
  "function": "() => {\n  const inputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input'));\n  const loc = inputs.find(i => (i.getAttribute('aria-label')||'').toLowerCase().includes('location'));\n  if (!loc) return 'no-loc';\n  const setter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window.HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set;\n  setter.call(loc, '');\n  loc.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));\n  loc.focus();\n  return loc.value;\n}"
}

}

{
  "function": "() => {\n  // Messenger renders each message as a row with aria-label describing sender/time/text\n  const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role=\"row\"]'));\n  const msgs = rows.map(r => r.getAttribute('aria-label') || r.innerText).filter(Boolean);\n  // Also grab any conversation header (listing title)\n  const main = document.querySelector('[role=\"main\"]');\n  return { count: msgs.length, msgs: msgs.slice(-40) };\n}"
}

{
  "function": "() => {\n  // Find the docked chat window containing the Ebrar/Stilton thread.\n  // Strategy: find an element whose text has many message-like lines incl. the listing title.\n  const candidates = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('div')).filter(d => {\n    const t = d.innerText || '';\n    return t.includes('Stilton') && t.includes('dinner with the kids');\n  });\n  // pick the smallest such container (most specific)\n  candidates.sort((a,b)=> (a.innerText.length - b.innerText.length));\n  const el = candidates[0];\n  return { found: candidates.length, text: el ? el.innerText.slice(0, 2500) : null };\n}"
}

  ]

```json
{
  "function": "() => {\n  const name = 'Mahfuzul';\n  const all = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role=\"button\"],button,[role=\"link\"],a,[role=\"gridcell\"],[role=\"row\"]'));\n  const matches = all.filter(b => (b.getAttribute('aria-label')||b.innerText||'').trim().startsWith(name));\n  if (!matches.length) {\n    // broaden: any element whose text starts with the name and mentions a listing\n    const els = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('div,span')).filter(e=>{\n      const t=(e.innerText||'').trim(); return t.startsWith(name+'\\n')||t.startsWith(name+' ');\n    });\n    return {err:'no role match', textMatchCount: els.length, firstText: els.length?els.sort((a,b)=>a.innerText.length-b.innerText.length)[0].innerText.slice(0,100):null};\n  }\n  return {roleMatches: matches.length, labels: matches.map(m=>(m.getAttribute('aria-label')||m.innerText||'').slice(0,60))};\n}"
}
```

## Skill Creator: Conventions & Process

**Skill location:** `/Users/anton/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/skill-creator/skills/skill-creator/`

### 1. **SKILL.md Location & Format**

The SKILL.md file is at: `/Users/anton/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/skill-creator/skills/skill-creator/SKILL.md`

Frontmatter format (YAML between `---` delimiters):
```yaml
---
name: skill-name
description: When to trigger, what it does. [Include triggering contexts here]
---
```

**Required fields:**
- `name`: Skill identifier (used as directory name too; kebab-case implied by convention)
- `description`: The primary triggering mechanism — includes both what the skill does AND explicit contexts for when to use it

**Description guidance** (critical for triggering):
- Must include "when to use" information
- Explicitly state contexts where the skill should trigger
- The SKILL.md advises being "pushy" — include phrases like "Make sure to use this skill whenever..." rather than just describing capability
- All "when to use" info goes in description, not in the body

**Optional fields mentioned:**
- `compatibility`: For required tools or dependencies (rarely needed)

### 2. **Step-by-Step Creation Process**

Skill-creator prescribes this workflow:

1. **Capture Intent** — Understand what the skill does and when it triggers
2. **Interview & Research** — Ask questions about edge cases, input/output formats, success criteria, dependencies
3. **Write the SKILL.md** — Fill in name, description, compatibility, and body content
4. **Write test cases** — Create 2-3 realistic prompts in `evals/evals.json` (don't write assertions yet)
5. **Spawn test runs in parallel** — For each test case, run WITH skill AND baseline (no skill) simultaneously
6. **Draft assertions while running** — Create quantitative checks in `eval_metadata.json`
7. **Grade outputs** — Evaluate assertions against actual outputs, save results to `grading.json`
8. **Aggregate benchmark** — Run `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py` to produce `benchmark.json`
9. **Launch viewer** — Use `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` to show results to user
10. **Iterate** — Get feedback, revise skill, rerun tests in new iteration directory
11. **Optimize description** (optional final step) — Run description optimization loop via `scripts/run_loop.py`

### 3. **Directory/Layout Conventions**

Standard skill structure:
```
skill-name/
├── SKILL.md (required)
├── scripts/          (optional: executable code for deterministic/repetitive tasks)
├── references/       (optional: documentation loaded into context as needed)
├── assets/           (optional: files used in output — templates, icons, fonts)
└── evals/           (optional: evaluation configs and test files)
    ├── evals.json   (test case definitions)
    ├── files/       (input files for evals)
    └── <test-files>
```

**File naming conventions:**
- Directories: kebab-case (implied)
- Scripts: Python files in `scripts/` directory, callable via subprocess
- References: `.md` files, referenced from SKILL.md with guidance on when to read them
- Assets: Any binary/template files needed for output

**Word count targets:**
- Metadata (name + description): ~100 words
- SKILL.md body: <500 lines (can exceed if needed, but add hierarchy and clear pointers)
- Reference files: Unlimited; for >300 lines, include table of contents

**Domain organization** (for multi-variant skills):
```
cloud-deploy/
├── SKILL.md
└── references/
    ├── aws.md
    ├── gcp.md
    └── azure.md
```

### 4. **Evals & Benchmarking**

**evals.json structure** (saved to `evals/evals.json`):
```json
{
  "skill_name": "example-skill",
  "evals": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "prompt": "User's example prompt",
      "expected_output": "Description of expected result",
      "files": ["evals/files/sample1.pdf"],
      "expectations": [
        "The output includes X",
        "The skill used script Y"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Test case workspace organization:**
```
<skill-name>-workspace/
├── iteration-1/
│   ├── eval-0-descriptive-name/
│   │   ├── with_skill/
│   │   │   └── outputs/
│   │   ├── without_skill/
│   │   │   └── outputs/
│   │   ├── eval_metadata.json
│   │   └── timing.json
│   ├── iteration-2/
│   └── benchmark.json
│   └── benchmark.md
```

**Assertions:**
- Should be objectively verifiable with descriptive names
- Read clearly in the benchmark viewer
- Subjective skills (writing style, design) often skip assertions
- Stored in `eval_metadata.json` with fields: `text`, `passed`, `evidence`

**Benchmark output** (`benchmark.json`):
- Generated by `scripts/aggregate_benchmark.py`
- Must use exact field names: `configuration` (not `config`), nested `result` object with `pass_rate`, `tokens`, `time_seconds`
- Includes per-config aggregates (mean ± stddev) and delta between with-skill vs. without-skill

### 5. **Evals/Benchmarking Component**

Skills creator **strongly emphasizes quantitative testing**:

- **With-skill vs. baseline runs** — Always compare WITH skill against a baseline (either no skill for new skills, or previous version for improvements)
- **Timing data** — Capture `total_tokens` and `duration_ms` from subagent task notifications immediately into `timing.json` (only available during notification, not recoverable later)
- **Grading process** — Spawn a grader subagent or grade inline, producing `grading.json` with expectations array using exact fields: `text`, `passed`, `evidence`
- **Variance analysis** — The `aggregate_benchmark.py` script computes mean ± stddev for pass_rate, time, and tokens
- **Analyst pass** — After aggregation, read patterns that aggregate stats might hide (non-discriminating assertions, flaky evals, time/token tradeoffs)
- **Blind comparison** (optional) — For rigorous A/B testing, use agents/comparator.md and agents/analyzer.md to have an independent agent compare two outputs without knowing which is which

### 6. **Description Triggering Guidance**

The skill-creator **strongly emphasizes description quality**:

- **Primary triggering mechanism** — Description is how Claude decides whether to invoke the skill
- **Undertrigger problem** — Claude tends to NOT use skills when they'd be useful, so descriptions should be "pushy"
- **Example of pushy description** — Instead of "How to build a simple fast dashboard to display internal data", write "How to build a simple fast dashboard to display internal data. Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions dashboards, data visualization, internal metrics, or wants to display any kind of company data, even if they don't explicitly ask for a 'dashboard.'"

**Description optimization loop** (optional, near end of development):
- Generate 20 trigger eval queries (mix of should-trigger and should-not-trigger)
- Review with user using `assets/eval_review.html` template
- Run `scripts/run_loop.py` which:
  - Splits evals into 60% train, 40% held-out test
  - Evaluates current description (3 runs per query for reliability)
  - Iterates up to 5 times, improving description based on failures
  - Returns `best_description` selected by test score (not train)

### 7. **Key Writing Principles**

From skill-creator's "Writing Style" section:

- **Explain the why** — Don't use all-caps MUST/NEVER; explain reasoning so the model understands importance
- **Imperative form** — Prefer imperative instructions
- **Progressive disclosure** — Load levels: metadata (always), SKILL.md body (on trigger), bundled resources (as needed)
- **Theory of mind** — Assume Claude is smart and has good theory of mind; good harnesses make it go beyond rote instructions
- **Output format definition** — Use structured templates with clear examples
- **Principle of lack of surprise** — No malware, exploit code, or misleading content

### Summary Table

| Aspect | Requirement |
|--------|-------------|
| **File structure** | `skill-name/SKILL.md` + optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`, `evals/` |
| **Frontmatter fields** | `name` (required), `description` (required), `compatibility` (optional) |
| **Description length** | ~100 words; include explicit "when to use" contexts |
| **SKILL.md body** | <500 lines; add hierarchy if longer |
| **Test cases** | 2-3 realistic prompts in `evals/evals.json`; don't pre-write assertions |
| **Assertions** | Objectively verifiable; stored with fields `text`, `passed`, `evidence` |
| **Benchmarking** | Always compare WITH skill vs. baseline; capture timing from task notifications |
| **Naming** | kebab-case for directories; Python for scripts |
| **Workspace org** | `<skill>-workspace/iteration-N/eval-<ID>/{with_skill,without_skill}/outputs/` |
```

**Simpler skills** (`resell-au-tracker`, `garage-sale`) contain **only** `SKILL.md` (no scripts, no tests).

---

### 3. **SKILL.md Frontmatter Format (Verbatim)**

#### **resell-au:**
```yaml
---
name: resell-au
description: >-
  Price secondhand items and write ready-to-post listings for selling in
  Australia (Facebook Marketplace or a garage sale), and optionally drive a
  real browser to fill the listing forms so the user only has to click Post.
  Use this skill WHENEVER the user wants to sell, flip, declutter, offload, or
  get rid of an item and asks what it's worth, how much to charge, how to
  price it, or wants a listing / title / description written — even if they
  just paste "selling X, condition Y" with no explicit question. Also trigger
  for "is this even worth selling", garage sale prep, batch-pricing a pile of
  stuff, "write me a Marketplace ad", or when the user points at a folder of
  photos and asks to list items automatically. Defaults to AUD and the
  Melbourne/Australian secondhand market. Always searches live comparable
  listings before pricing.
---
```

#### **resell-au-tracker:**
```yaml
---
name: resell-au-tracker
description: >-
  Sync items from resell-au listing.md files into tracker.json
  (~/Desktop/things-for-sale/tracker.json). Use when the user says "sync
  tracker", "update the tracker", "add my listings to the tracker", or after
  the resell-au skill has published new listings. Non-destructive: never
  modifies existing rows or sold prices.
---
```

#### **garage-sale:**
```yaml
---
name: garage-sale
description: >-
  Generate a print-ready HTML garage sale label sheet from listing.md files.
  Scans a folder of item subfolders, reads each listing.md for the Marketplace
  price and garage sale price, and outputs an A4 HTML label sheet showing the
  original listed price and the marked-down garage sale price side-by-side.
  Use this skill whenever the user mentions a garage sale, wants price labels,
  wants to print tags, or says anything like "mark everything down", "I'm having
  a garage sale", or "print labels for my listings". Requires listing.md files
  produced by the resell-au skill.
---
```

**Format:** Simple YAML frontmatter with `name:` (string) and `description:` (multiline, folded `>-`). No other fields used. The description is the **trigger clause**—it explains when the skill should be invoked.

---

### 4. **Runtime Path References**

Scripts reference their own location and the repo root **relative to their position**:

**Example from `refresh_r0_classify.py` (line 32):**
```python
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from refresh_pricing import proposed_price
```

**From tests (line 16–19 in `check_refresh_pricing.sh`):**
```bash
DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_ROOT="$(cd "$DIR/.." && pwd)"
cd "$SKILL_ROOT"
```

**Convention:** Scripts assume they live in `<skill>/scripts/` and use `os.path.abspath(__file__)` + relative traversal (`.` or `..`) to locate siblings and the repo root. This works whether the skill is at the repo or symlinked in `~/.claude/skills/`.

**SKILL.md references to scripts:** Refer to them as `<skill_dir>/scripts/<name>.py` (line 468 in resell-au SKILL.md):
```
python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/refresh_r0_classify.py <target_folder>
```

At runtime, the agent expands `<skill_dir>` to the absolute path of the installed/symlinked skill directory.

---

### 5. **Flat-Layout Convention for the Repo**

**Confirmed structure:**
```
/Users/anton/src/agent-skills/
├── <skill_name>/
│   ├── SKILL.md                   [Required. Frontmatter + body.]
│   ├── references/                [Optional. Markdown reference docs.]
│   ├── scripts/                   [Optional. Python utilities.]
│   └── tests/                     [Optional. Unit + integration tests.]
├── AGENTS.md                      [Repo-wide governance + conventions]
├── CLAUDE.md                      [Imports AGENTS.md + Claude-Code notes]
└── .mise.toml                     [Python version pinning]
```

**For a new skill:**
1. Create `/Users/anton/src/agent-skills/<new-skill-name>/SKILL.md`
2. Optionally add `references/`, `scripts/`, `tests/` subdirectories as needed
3. The symlink in `~/.claude/skills/` will be created automatically by Claude Code's skill discovery (no manual step required)
4. **No CLAUDE.md or tests are required per skill**—skills are standalone directories

---

### 6. **Python Pinning & Testing**

**`.mise.toml` (repo root):**
```toml
[tools]
python = "3.14"
```

All scripts run under this pinned version. To verify:
```bash
cd /Users/anton/src/agent-skills
mise trust
mise install
python3 --version  # → Python 3.14.x
```

**Golden-test pattern** (resell-au only):
- **Unit tests:** `tests/test_refresh_pricing.py`, `tests/test_refresh_runstate.py` (pure logic, no I/O)
- **Integration fixtures:** `tests/fixtures/refresh-r0/`, `tests/fixtures/refresh-r2/` (input + `.golden.txt` / `.golden/` outputs)
- **Regression runners:** `tests/check_*.sh` scripts call the python tests and compare classifier output against golden

Example run:
```bash
cd /Users/anton/src/agent-skills/resell-au
./tests/check_refresh_pricing.sh       # Runs unit tests
./tests/check_refresh_r0.sh            # Runs classifier against fixture, diffs .golden.txt
```

# Plan: `resell-au-pickups` skill

## Context

This session we manually swept the user's Facebook Marketplace inbox, read every
buyer conversation, and produced a Melbourne-timezone summary of who is picking up
what, when, where, and for how much — then generated calendar entries (Google
Calendar MCP, falling back to a `.ics` import file when the connector turned out to
be read-only). The user wants this codified as a **reusable skill** so the whole
flow runs on command instead of by hand.

It joins the existing `resell-au` family (`resell-au`, `resell-au-tracker`,
`garage-sale`) as a new **standalone** skill, invoked `/resell-au-pickups`. The repo
`/Users/anton/src/agent-skills` is source-of-truth; `~/.claude/skills/*` are symlinks,
so creating the dir here makes it live (discovery auto-symlinks).

Non-obvious techniques discovered this session that MUST be captured (they are what
make the automation work and are easy to get wrong):
- The Marketplace inbox renders a clicked conversation as a **docked Messenger chat
  window**, not an inline pane. The dock caps at ~5 windows — opening a 6th silently
  fails. Must close docked windows between reads.
- Message extraction: find the composer `[aria-label^="Write to "]`, walk ~15
  ancestors up, parse `innerText` lines matching
  `^Enter, Message sent (.+?) by ([^:]+?): ([\s\S]*)$`. Price = the line containing `AU$`.
- The inbox **reorders** when a new message arrives mid-sweep, so a11y-snapshot `uid`s
  go stale. Click rows by **buyer name** via a DOM query, not by cached uid.
- Calendar: the claude.ai Google Calendar connector may be **read-only**
  (`insufficient authentication scopes` on `create_event`). Always have the `.ics`
  fallback. June in Melbourne is AEST (UTC+10, no DST) — but emit a proper
  `VTIMEZONE` for `Australia/Melbourne` so it is correct year-round.

 .replace(\";\", \"\\\\;\")\n        .replace(\",\", \"\\\\,\")\n        .replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\\\n\")\n        .replace(\"\\n\", \"\\\\n\")\n        .replace(\"\\r\", \"\\\\n\")\n    )\n\n\ndef {
  "file_path": "/Users/anton/src/agent-skills/resell-au-pickups/references/inbox-extraction.md",
  "content": "# Inbox extraction — Facebook Marketplace messages\n\nHow to read every buyer conversation out of the Marketplace inbox with the\nChrome DevTools MCP, and how to classify what you find. These are the\nhard-won details — the inbox does not behave like a normal page.\n\nAll snippets run via `evaluate_script` on the attached Chrome (port 9222).\n\n## The inbox is a dock, not a reading pane\n\nNavigating to `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/inbox` shows the list of\nconversations on the left. **Clicking a conversation does NOT open an inline\nreading pane** — it opens a docked Messenger chat window (a \"chat head\") at the\nbottom of the screen. Two consequences:\n\n1. The thread text lives in that docked window, anchored by its message\n   composer, not in `[role=\"main\"]`.\n2. **The dock caps at ~5 open windows.** Once five are open, clicking a sixth\n   silently does nothing. So you must **close docked windows between reads** or\n   the sweep stalls with no error.\n\nWork **one conversation at a time**: close all docked windows → click the next\nrow → wait ~3 s → extract → repeat.\n\n### Close all docked windows\n\n```js\n() => { Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[aria-label^=\"Close chat\"]'))\n  .forEach(b => { try { b.click() } catch (e) {} }); return 'closed'; }\n```\n\n## Click a row by buyer name (never by snapshot uid)\n\nThe inbox **reorders the moment a new message arrives** mid-sweep, so any `uid`\ncaptured from an earlier `take_snapshot` goes stale and you will open the wrong\nthread. Click rows by buyer name via a DOM query instead:\n\n```js\n() => {\n  const name = 'Cindy';                       // buyer's display name\n  const el = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role=\"button\"],button'))\n    .find(b => (b.getAttribute('aria-label') || b.innerText || '').trim().startsWith(name));\n  if (!el) return { err: 'not found' };\n  el.click();\n  return { clicked: true };\n}\n```\n\nTo get the list of names to iterate, take ONE snapshot of the inbox up front and\nread the row labels (each row reads `\"<Name>   <listing title> <last-msg> <time>\"`).\nTreat that list as your work-queue, but always click by name, and if a new row\nappears at the top (a fresh message) re-read the queue.\n\n## Extract a thread\n\nAfter clicking, the docked window mounts a composer with\n`aria-label=\"Write to <Name> · <listing title>\"`. Anchor on it, walk up ~15\nancestors to the window root, and parse the message lines. Facebook renders each\nmessage with a hidden label `Enter, Message sent <when> by <who>: <text>`:\n\n```js\n() => {\n  const composers = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[contenteditable=\"true\"],[role=\"textbox\"]'))\n    .filter(e => (e.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Write to '));\n  if (!composers.length) return { err: 'no open chat' };\n  const composer = composers[0];\n  const thread = composer.getAttribute('aria-label').replace(/^Write to /, '');\n  let big = composer;\n  for (let i = 0; i < 15; i++) { if (big.parentElement) big = big.parentElement; }\n  const lines = (big.innerText || '').split('\\n');\n  const msgs = [];\n  const re = /^Enter, Message sent (.+?) by ([^:]+?): ([\\s\\S]*)$/;\n  for (const ln of lines) { const m = ln.match(re); if (m) msgs.push(m[1] + ' — ' + m[2] + ': ' + m[3]); }\n  const price = lines.find(l => /AU\\$/.test(l));   // listing price header, e.g. \"AU$35 – <title>\"\n  return { thread, price, msgs };\n}\n```\n\nNotes:\n- `msgs` comes out in chronological order: `\"<when> — <You|Buyer>: <text>\"`.\n  `<when>` is FB's own relative/absolute stamp (\"Tuesday 7:45pm\", \"8:38 AM\",\n  \"May 27, 2026, 11:55 AM\") — keep it; it anchors date resolution.\n- `price` is the **listing** price (the AU$ header). The agreed price may differ\n  if they haggled — read the messages for the final figure.\n- If `msgs` is empty but a composer exists, the thread is still loading — wait\n  another 2 s and re-run.\n- If there is **no** composer at all, the click didn't land (dock full, or the\n  name matched a stale row) — close all windows and re-click by name.\n\n## One thing to avoid\n\nDon't try to read threads from the top-bar Messenger drawer or the Notifications\nflyout — those are separate overlays and contain your general Messenger chats,\nnot the Marketplace buyer threads. If `evaluate_script` starts returning\n\"Notifications\" / \"Chats\" text, press `Escape` and re-navigate to\n`/marketplace/inbox`.\n\n## Classification rubric\n\nBucket each thread from its messages:\n\n- **confirmed** — a day AND a time are agreed by both sides (\"Saturday ~9am?\" →\n  \"yeah that's fine\"). Goes in the calendar.\n- **agreed-time-TBC** — both want to trade and a day is loosely set but no firm\n  time (\"tomorrow morning\" with no hour, or you proposed and they haven't\n  replied with a time). Worth a calendar hold marked TBC + a nudge.\n- **declined / dead** — haggle stalled below your floor, buyer bought elsewhere,\n  or either side said no.\n- **inquiry-only** — \"is this still available?\" with no arrangement.\n\nFor each confirmed/TBC item capture: **buyer**, **item**, **date** (resolved —\nsee below), **time**, **agreed price**, **location**, and any **action note**\n(\"text before leaving\", \"have it ready by the door\", \"leaving cash in the\ndrawer / PayID\").\n\n### Resolve relative dates\n\nFB stamps and buyer phrasing are relative. Resolve against **today in\nMelbourne**:\n\n- \"tonight\" → today's date.\n- \"tomorrow\" → today + 1.\n- a weekday name (\"Friday\") → the next occurrence of that weekday (today if it\n  *is* that weekday and the time is still ahead).\n- A stamp like \"Tuesday 7:45pm\" on a message is when it was *sent* — use it only\n  to order messages, not as the pickup date; the pickup date comes from the\n  agreement text.\n\n### Pickup vs delivery location\n\n- **Delivery** (buyer asked you to drop off) → location is the **buyer's\n  address**, which they'll have pasted in the thread.\n- **Pickup** (buyer collects) → location is the **seller's address** if it\n  appears in the thread; otherwise leave it as \"your place\" — **never hardcode\n  an address**.\n"
}

  "content": "# Calendar export — MCP first, ICS fallback\n\nTwo ways to get pickups into the user's calendar. Try the Google Calendar MCP\nfirst; fall back to a generated `.ics` the moment it's unavailable or read-only.\n\n## Path A — Google Calendar MCP (`create_event`)\n\nOne call per event. Map the captured pickup fields like this:\n\n| `create_event` arg  | Value |\n|---------------------|-------|\n| `summary`           | `\"<Buyer> — <item> ($<price>)\"`, e.g. `\"Cindy — fog machine ($35)\"` |\n| `startTime`         | naive local, `\"2026-06-04T18:00:00\"` |\n| `endTime`           | start + 30 min (pickup) or + 60 min (a delivery you drive to) |\n| `timeZone`          | `\"Australia/Melbourne\"` (always — dictates display TZ) |\n| `location`          | buyer address for a delivery; seller address (or omit) for a pickup |\n| `description`       | agreed price, payment note, and any action (\"text before leaving\", \"have it ready\") |\n| `overrideReminders` | `[{\"method\":\"popup\",\"minutes\":30}]` for pickups; `45` for a delivery drive |\n| `colorId`           | optional — `\"11\"` (tomato) reads well for a delivery you have to leave for |\n\nFor a **TBC** event, still create it at a best-guess time, prefix the summary\nwith the day and `(TBC)`, and put \"TIME NOT CONFIRMED — confirm with <buyer>\" in\nthe description so it's obvious when it surfaces.\n\n### The read-only failure to watch for\n\nThe claude.ai Google Calendar connector is frequently connected **read-only**.\n`list_calendars` / `list_events` succeed, but `create_event` returns:\n\n```\nRequest had insufficient authentication scopes.\n```\n\nIf you see this (or there is no Calendar MCP at all), **stop retrying** and\nswitch to Path B. A `/mcp` reconnect does *not* fix it unless the user re-grants\nthe calendar *edit* scope on Google's consent screen — so don't loop on it.\nMention the read-only cause once, then hand over the `.ics`.\n\n## Path B — generate a `.ics` with `make_ics.py`\n\nBuild a JSON array of event objects and pipe it through the script. Each object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"uid\": \"resell-<buyer>-<item>@things-for-sale\",\n  \"summary\": \"Cindy - fog machine pickup ($35)\",\n  \"start\": \"2026-06-04T18:00:00\",\n  \"end\": \"2026-06-04T18:30:00\",\n  \"location\": \"2/35-37 Grange Road, Caulfield East VIC\",\n  \"description\": \"Fog machine, fluid included. $35 cash. She'll message when on her way.\",\n  \"alarm_minutes\": 30\n}\n```\n\nRun it (default folder is the resell-au working folder):\n\n```bash\npython3 <skill_dir>/scripts/make_ics.py events.json --out ~/Desktop/things-for-sale/pickups.ics\n# or stream: cat events.json | python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/make_ics.py > pickups.ics\n```\n\nThe script emits a single `VCALENDAR` carrying an `Australia/Melbourne`\n`VTIMEZONE` (correct year-round, AEST↔AEDT), one `VEVENT` per item, a `VALARM`\nfor any event with `alarm_minutes`, RFC-5545 text escaping, and 75-octet line\nfolding. Output is deterministic (fixed `DTSTAMP`, UIDs from input) so it stays\ngolden-testable. `start`/`end` are naive local Melbourne times — do **not**\npre-convert to UTC.\n\n### Tell the user how to import\n\n1. Open **calendar.google.com** → ⚙️ **Settings** → **Import & Export**.\n2. Under *Import*, **Select file** → choose `pickups.ics`.\n3. Pick the calendar → **Import** (\"N events imported\").\n\n(Double-clicking the file on macOS imports into Apple Calendar instead — fine if\nthat's what they use.)\n"
}

  "content": "---\nname: resell-au-pickups\ndescription: >-\n  Sweep your Facebook Marketplace inbox, read every buyer conversation, and\n  summarise which items are being collected — who, what day and time, for how\n  much, and where (pickup vs delivery) — then optionally add the pickups to your\n  calendar. Use this skill WHENEVER the user wants to check their Marketplace / FB\n  messages, asks who is picking up what and when, wants pickup or delivery times\n  pulled out of their chats, or says things like \"go through my messages\", \"what\n  have I agreed to\", \"which items are people picking up and on what dates\", or\n  \"put my pickups in my calendar\". Defaults to Melbourne, Australia timezone and\n  AUD. Pairs with the resell-au skill.\n---\n\n# Resell AU — Pickups\n\nRead the user's Facebook Marketplace buyer conversations and turn them into a\nclear picture of what's being collected, by whom, when, where, and for how much —\nthen, on request, drop those pickups into their calendar.\n\nThe user is in **Melbourne, Australia**: times are **AEST/AEDT**, money is\n**AUD**, and most trades are local cash/PayID pickups (sometimes a paid drop-off).\n\nStanding preferences (already decided — don't re-ask):\n\n- **Melbourne timezone** for every time you report or schedule.\n- **Never hardcode an address.** Read the pickup/delivery address out of the\n  thread. If a pickup has no stated address, say \"your place\" rather than guess.\n- **Be honest about certainty.** Separate what's actually agreed from what's\n  still loose — don't promote a \"maybe\" into a booking.\n\nThis is a read-and-summarise skill. It does **not** mark items sold, reply to\nbuyers, or change listings unless the user explicitly asks (then defer to the\n`resell-au` skill for listing changes).\n\n---\n\n## Workflow\n\n### Phase 0 — Pre-flight\n\n1. Confirm Chrome is attached on port 9222 via a `list_pages` MCP call. If it\n   isn't, surface the `resell-au` skill's `references/chrome-setup.md` and stop.\n2. Navigate to `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/inbox` and confirm the user\n   is logged in (you'll see the Selling/Buying tabs and a list of\n   conversations). If not, ask them to log in once in the attached Chrome.\n\n### Phase 1 — Sweep the inbox\n\nRead **every** conversation that looks like it could involve an arrangement\n(skip pure \"is this available?\" with no reply only at classification time, not\nnow — read them so you can classify accurately).\n\nPer the full recipe in `references/inbox-extraction.md`:\n\n1. Take one snapshot to get the list of buyer names + listing titles — this is\n   your work-queue.\n2. For each buyer, **one at a time**: close all docked chat windows → click the\n   row **by buyer name** (not by snapshot uid) → wait ~3 s → run the\n   composer-anchored extractor to pull the message history + listing price.\n3. If the inbox reorders (a new message jumps to the top), re-read the queue.\n\nKey gotchas (all covered in the reference): clicking opens a docked Messenger\nwindow, the dock caps at ~5 so you must close between reads, and snapshot uids\ngo stale on reorder so you click by name.\n\n### Phase 2 — Classify & resolve\n\nFor each thread, bucket it: **confirmed** (day + time agreed), **agreed-time-TBC**,\n**declined/dead**, or **inquiry-only**. For every confirmed / TBC item capture:\n\n- **buyer**, **item**, **agreed price** (the negotiated figure if they haggled,\n  not just the listing price),\n- **date** — resolve relative phrasing (\"tonight\", \"tomorrow\", \"Friday\")\n  to an absolute Melbourne date from today,\n- **time** (or \"morning/daytime — TBC\"),\n- **location** — buyer's address for a delivery, seller's address (or \"your\n  place\") for a pickup,\n- **action note** — \"text before leaving\", \"have it ready by the door\", cash /\n  PayID instructions.\n\nThe classification rubric and date-resolution rules live in\n`references/inbox-extraction.md`.\n\n### Phase 3 — Summary\n\nPresent a tight, scannable summary grouped by day, newest first, Melbourne times.\nUse these sections (drop any that are empty):\n\n- **🔴 Locked-in — happening soon** — the next 1–2 confirmed trades, with the\n  action note called out (e.g. \"you drive — text before leaving\").\n- **Per-day tables** — one small table per day: Time · Item · Buyer · $ ·\n  (pickup/deliver). Put pickups at the same address together.\n- **🟡 Agreed but time TBC — needs a nudge** — who to message to pin a time.\n- **⚪ Done / dead** — already collected, declined, or bought elsewhere — one line\n  each so the user knows you saw them.\n\nClose with a one-line **week at a glance**. Flag clashes (two pickups at the same\naddress within an hour) and anything that needs the user to leave the house.\n\n### Phase 4 — Calendar (optional — ask first)\n\nAsk whether to add the pickups to their calendar. If yes, build the event list\nand follow `references/calendar-export.md`:\n\n- **Try the Google Calendar MCP `create_event`** first — one event per pickup,\n  `timeZone: \"Australia/Melbourne\"`, a popup reminder (30 min for a pickup, 45\n  min for a delivery you drive to), price + action note in the description.\n- **If `create_event` returns `insufficient authentication scopes`** (the\n  connector is read-only) or there's no Calendar MCP, **stop retrying** and fall\n  back to `scripts/make_ics.py`: write `pickups.ics` into the target folder\n  (default `~/Desktop/things-for-sale`) and give the import steps.\n\nMark TBC events clearly (prefix the day + `(TBC)`, note \"confirm time\" in the\ndescription) so they're unmistakable when they pop up.\n\nOffer, but don't assume: replying to buyers to lock TBC times is a separate\naction — only do it if the user says so.\n\n---\n\n## Files\n\n- `references/inbox-extraction.md` — the browser/DOM technique for reading\n  threads, dock management, click-by-name, the extractor, and the classification\n  + date-resolution rules.\n- `references/calendar-export.md` — `create_event` field mapping, the read-only\n  fallback, and the `make_ics.py` interface.\n- `scripts/make_ics.py` — JSON pickup events → a valid `Australia/Melbourne`\n  `.ics` with reminders. Deterministic; covered by `tests/check_make_ics.sh`.\n"
